# Making Charges on Gold Jewellery: Per Gram, Percentage and Wastage Explained
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/making-charges-explained

How jewellers charge making: per gram, as a percentage, flat per piece, or as wastage. Worked examples, what to show on the bill, and how to stay consistent.

GUIDE · PRICING

## Making charges explained

 Per gram, percentage, flat or wastage: four ways to charge for the same work. Which suits which piece, how each looks on the bill, and how to keep every counter quoting the same.

 See live-rate billing 

 Pricing · 6 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## Four ways to charge for the same work

 On a 10 gram 22K piece at ₹6,875 a gram (metal value ₹68,750):

 Percentage of metal value , say 12%: ₹8,250. Rises and falls with the gold rate.

 Per gram , say ₹600 a gram: ₹6,000. Stays the same when the rate moves, so it is easier to quote.

 Flat per piece , say ₹1,500: suits light, machine-made items where weight varies little.

 Wastage or value addition , say 8% of weight: 0.8 g × ₹6,875 = ₹5,500. Charged in grams, so it also moves with the rate.

## Which suits which piece

 Chains, coins and machine-made pieces: per gram or flat. Customers compare these across shops, and a simple number wins.

 Handmade, antique, temple and bridal: percentage or wastage. The work is in the craft, and the charge should grow with the piece.

 Studded jewellery: making on the metal, with stones priced separately.

## What to show on the bill

 Show gross weight, net weight, purity, the rate, metal value, making, stones and GST on separate lines. BIS hallmarking rules ask for net weight, purity and the hallmarking charge to be shown. Making on its own line is what stops the “why is this so much?” conversation.

## Making, GST and job work

 On a piece you sell, making is part of the sale and carries 3% GST with it. Making on gold the customer brings is job work, billed as a service. See the GST guide .

## Discounts on making

 “Up to 50% off making” is the most common festive offer. Decide in advance which categories it covers, who can approve more, and whether it applies to wastage too. A discount given differently at two counters costs margin and trust.

## How Jwero does it

 In Jwero, making is part of each product’s price setup, and the counter quote, the catalogue and the website price all use it. Discounts beyond what a salesperson may give can be sent to a manager for approval at the counter. See billing and the price calculator .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 What is a normal making charge on gold jewellery? 
 It varies widely by design, city and shop: machine-made chains carry low making, while handmade, antique and bridal work carry much more. There is no standard rate; set yours by category and apply it consistently.

 Is wastage the same as making charge? 
 It is the same idea expressed differently. Wastage, or value addition, is a percentage added to the weight and charged at the gold rate; making is usually charged in rupees. Some shops charge both.

 Should making be shown separately on the bill? 
 Showing it separately builds trust and avoids disputes. Under BIS hallmarking rules, the bill should show the net weight, purity and hallmarking charge separately; most jewellers show making on its own line too.

## One making rule, every counter.

 Set making once in Jwero and every counter, the website and WhatsApp quote it the same way.

# Old Gold Exchange: How Jewellers Value It, Deductions and Paperwork
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/old-gold-exchange-jewellers

How to value old gold for exchange or buyback: purity testing, stone deduction, net weight, today’s rate, the paperwork to keep, and cash payout limits.

GUIDE · OLD GOLD

## Old gold exchange: valuing it fairly

 Test it, weigh it, take out the stones, apply today’s rate, and write it all down. The counter process that keeps exchange fair to the customer and safe for the shop.

 See old gold at the counter 

 Counter · 7 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## The formula

 Old gold value = net weight × tested purity × today’s buying rate − your stated deduction 

 Example: a 12 gram bangle with 1.5 grams of stones, tested at 22K, buying rate ₹6,700 a gram for 22K. Net weight 10.5 g × ₹6,700 = ₹70,350, before any deduction.

## Step 1: test the purity

 Use a karat meter (XRF) if you have one; a touchstone test is common but less exact. Test in front of the customer and show the reading. A hallmarked piece with a HUID tells you the declared purity, but test anyway: old pieces are often repaired with lower-karat solder.

## Step 2: weigh and take out the stones

 Weigh gross, then deduct stones, beads, lac and anything that is not gold. Write both weights on the voucher. This is where most exchange disputes start, so do it where the customer can see the scale.

## Step 3: apply today’s rate and your deduction

 Use your buying rate for the tested purity. If your shop deducts for melting and refining loss, state the percentage before you test, not after. Shops that are open about the deduction lose fewer customers over it.

## Step 4: exchange or buyback

 Exchange: the value becomes a credit against a new piece. Issue a voucher and apply it on the new bill.

 Buyback: you pay the customer. Larger amounts should go by bank transfer; cash expenses above ₹10,000 to one person in a day can be disallowed for income tax.

## The paperwork to keep

 Customer name, phone and ID

 PAN or Form 60 for amounts above ₹2 lakh

 Gross weight, stone weight, net weight, tested purity, rate and deduction

 A purchase voucher signed by the customer

 GST is charged on the new piece; see the GST guide for how the exchange affects it.

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero handles old gold as a voucher at the counter: the exchange credit is applied against the new purchase. Buybacks record the stone-weight deduction, go through an approve and settle step, and produce a voucher document, with cash payout limits checked before settlement. Old gold can also be redeemed into a gold scheme . See the counter .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 How is old gold valued? 
 Old gold value = net weight after removing stones × tested purity (karat ÷ 24) × today’s buying rate, less any deduction your shop applies for melting and refining.

 Why do jewellers deduct from old gold? 
 Old pieces often contain solder and alloys, and lose some weight when melted and refined. Shops apply a deduction for this. Tell the customer the deduction before testing, and print it on the voucher.

 Can I pay cash for old gold? 
 Cash payouts are limited. Cash expenses above ₹10,000 to one person in a day can be disallowed for income tax, so larger buybacks are better paid by bank transfer. Confirm with your CA.

 Do I need the customer’s PAN? 
 For a purchase above ₹2 lakh, record the customer’s PAN or Form 60. For every purchase, keep their name, ID and a signed voucher.

## Old gold, valued the same way every time.

 Jwero records the test, the stone deduction and the value, issues the voucher, and applies it against the new bill.

# Cash and PAN Rules for Jewellers: ₹2 Lakh, Section 269ST and PMLA
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/cash-limit-pan-jewellery-sale

When a jeweller needs PAN or Form 60, the ₹2 lakh cash limit under Section 269ST, cash payouts, and the ₹10 lakh PMLA rule for dealers in precious metals.

GUIDE · COMPLIANCE

## Cash and PAN rules for jewellers

 Three numbers every counter should know: PAN above ₹2 lakh, no cash receipt of ₹2 lakh or more, and the ₹10 lakh cash rule for dealers in precious metals and stones.

 See how Jwero handles compliance 

 Compliance · 7 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## The three numbers

 Above ₹2 lakh: record PAN or Form 60 for the sale or purchase.

 ₹2 lakh or more in cash: you must not receive it from one person in a day, for one transaction, or for one event.

 ₹10 lakh or more in cash: PMLA obligations for dealers in precious metals and stones.

 Check with your CA. These are legal obligations with penalties. Use this page to brief your team, and your CA for how they apply to your business. Rules here are as we understand them in October 2026; tax and compliance rules change, and your CA’s reading of your business comes first.

## PAN or Form 60 above ₹2 lakh

 Rule 114B of the Income-tax Rules requires PAN for a sale or purchase of goods above ₹2 lakh in a transaction, whatever the mode of payment. If the customer has no PAN, they fill Form 60. This applies to buying old gold too. Record it on the bill, not on a separate sheet.

## Section 269ST: the cash receipt limit

 You must not receive ₹2 lakh or more in cash:

 from one person in one day, in total;

 for one transaction; or

 for transactions relating to one event or occasion, such as a wedding.

 The penalty under Section 271DA is equal to the amount received, and it falls on the jeweller who receives the cash, not the customer. Splitting a ₹3 lakh bill into two cash bills on the same day does not avoid it.

## Paying out cash

 On the other side, cash expenses above ₹10,000 to one person in a day can be disallowed for income tax (Section 40A(3)). For old gold buybacks above that, pay by bank transfer.

## PMLA: the ₹10 lakh rule

 Since December 2020, dealers in precious metals and stones are reporting entities under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act for cash transactions of ₹10 lakh or more, including linked transactions. In practice that means customer due diligence (KYC), keeping records, registering with FIU-IND and reporting as required. Your CA will tell you what applies at your size.

## What to train the counter on

 Ask for PAN before billing above ₹2 lakh, not after.

 Add up the day’s cash from the same customer before taking more.

 Treat a wedding purchase over several visits as one event.

 Never pay cash above ₹10,000 for a buyback.

## What Jwero does today

 Jwero keeps KYC records in a protected vault and contains the rules for PAN above ₹2 lakh and the PMLA ₹10 lakh threshold. Today the cash limit is enforced on old gold buybacks; it does not yet block a cash payment at counter checkout, so the counter still needs to follow the rule. See security and compliance .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 When does a jeweller need the customer’s PAN? 
 For a sale or purchase of goods above ₹2 lakh in one transaction, record the customer’s PAN, or Form 60 if they do not have one (Rule 114B of the Income-tax Rules).

 How much cash can a jeweller accept? 
 Section 269ST says you must not receive ₹2 lakh or more in cash from one person in a day, for one transaction, or for one event. The penalty under Section 271DA equals the amount received.

 Can a customer split a cash payment over two bills? 
 Splitting does not help. The limit applies to the total from one person in a day and to all payments for one event, such as a wedding purchase.

 What is the PMLA rule for jewellers? 
 Dealers in precious metals and stones are reporting entities under PMLA for cash transactions of ₹10 lakh or more, including linked transactions. That brings KYC, record-keeping and reporting to FIU-IND. Confirm your obligations with your CA.

# HUID Hallmarking Rules for Jewellers: What to Check Before Every Sale
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/huid-hallmarking-rules-jewellers

Mandatory hallmarking and the 6-digit HUID: which pieces need it, the exemptions, what the customer can verify, and what the counter should check before billing.

GUIDE · HALLMARKING

## HUID hallmarking: what to check before every sale

 Which gold pieces need a HUID, who is exempt, how customers check it on their phone, and the three checks your counter should make before a hallmarked piece is billed.

 See HUID in Jwero 

 Compliance · 6 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## The rule in brief

 Gold jewellery and artefacts sold in the districts notified by BIS must be hallmarked, and since 1 April 2023 the hallmark must carry a 6-digit alphanumeric HUID (Hallmark Unique Identification). A hallmark has three marks: the BIS logo, the purity grade (for example 22K916) and the HUID.

 Check with your CA. Hallmarking rules, notified districts and exemptions are set by BIS and do change. Check the BIS website for the current position. Rules here are as we understand them in October 2026; tax and compliance rules change, and your CA’s reading of your business comes first.

## Which purities are hallmarked

 Gold jewellery is hallmarked in set grades, including 14K, 18K, 20K, 22K, 23K and 24K. A piece outside these grades cannot be hallmarked as gold jewellery.

## Exemptions

 At the time of writing, the main exemptions are jewellers with annual turnover up to ₹40 lakh and articles under 2 grams. If you rely on an exemption, keep the basis for it on file.

## What the customer can check

 Customers can enter the HUID in the BIS CARE app and see the purity, the article type and the hallmarking centre. More customers do this every year, especially for bridal purchases. A mismatch at the counter loses the sale and the customer’s trust.

## Three checks before billing a hallmarked piece

 The HUID is in your stock record and matches the one on the piece.

 The purity on the bill matches the hallmark. A 22K916 piece billed as 22K at a different rate is a dispute waiting to happen.

 The HUID is not on another piece in your records. Duplicates are usually typing errors, but they need to be fixed before sale.

## Keeping the records

 Record the HUID when the piece comes back from the hallmarking centre, not at the counter. Track hallmarking batches: which pieces went out, when they came back, and which failed. Our HUID records and audit checklist covers the record-keeping in detail.

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero stores a HUID on each piece and will not accept the same HUID on two pieces. Hallmarking batches are tracked going out and coming back. At the counter, a hallmark check can be set to off, warn or block, and blocks by default where hallmarking is mandatory. See inventory .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 Is HUID mandatory on gold jewellery? 
 Hallmarking with a 6-digit HUID is mandatory for gold jewellery and artefacts sold in the districts notified by BIS. Check the current list of districts on the BIS website.

 Who is exempt from mandatory hallmarking? 
 At the time of writing, jewellers with annual turnover up to ₹40 lakh, and articles weighing under 2 grams, among a few other exemptions. Confirm the current exemptions with BIS.

 How can a customer check a HUID? 
 With the BIS CARE app: entering the HUID shows the purity, the type of article and the hallmarking centre.

 Can two pieces have the same HUID? 
 No. Each HUID is unique to one piece. A duplicate in your stock means a data entry error or a problem piece, and should be checked before sale.

## No unhallmarked piece billed by mistake.

 Jwero checks the HUID at the counter, and can warn or block the sale when it is missing.

# E-Way Bill for Jewellery: Is Gold Exempt? Delivery Challans and State Rules
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/e-way-bill-for-jewellery

Jewellery under Chapter 71 is exempt from the GST e-way bill under Rule 138(14), but some states require it for intra-state gold movement. Plus delivery challans.

GUIDE · GST

## E-way bill for jewellery

 Jewellery is on the national exemption list, so most movements need no e-way bill. But some states have their own rule for gold, and every movement still needs a challan or invoice.

 See memo and dispatch in Jwero 

 Accounts and GST · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## The short answer

 Under the GST e-way bill rules, goods under Chapter 71 (natural or cultured pearls, precious and semi-precious stones, precious metals and jewellery) are on the list of goods that do not need an e-way bill (Rule 138(14) and its annexure). Most jewellery movements across India need no e-way bill.

 Check with your CA. State rules for intra-state movement of gold differ and change. Confirm the rule for your state before you rely on the exemption. Rules here are as we understand them in October 2026; tax and compliance rules change, and your CA’s reading of your business comes first.

## The exception: state rules

 States can notify their own requirements for movement within the state. Kerala, for example, has notified an e-way bill for intra-state movement of gold and precious stones above a set value. If you move stock within such a state, follow its rule.

## No e-way bill still means paperwork

 Every movement of goods needs a document travelling with it:

 A tax invoice when it is a sale.

 A delivery challan when it is not a sale: gold to a karigar or job-work unit, pieces sent on approval, stock to an exhibition, or a transfer to another branch.

 The challan should show the items, weights and purity. Goods sent on approval or for job work should come back, or be billed, against it.

## Where jewellers lose track

 Pieces out on approval with no record of what came back.

 Exhibition stock counted out but not counted back in.

 Karigar issues recorded in grams of jewellery, not fine grams.

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero records approval memos, memo issues, consignments, dispatch and exhibition stock, so each movement has a document, and what went out is matched against what came back or was billed. Karigar issues and receipts are recorded by fine weight. See inventory and manufacturing .

# E-Invoicing for Jewellers: Who Must Issue It, B2B vs B2C, and the 30-Day Rule
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/e-invoicing-for-jewellers

E-invoicing applies to B2B invoices for businesses above ₹5 crore turnover. What jewellers selling to the trade need to do, and why retail bills are different.

GUIDE · GST

## E-invoicing for jewellers

 If you sell to other businesses and your turnover is above ₹5 crore, your B2B invoices need an IRN. Retail bills to customers do not. Here is how it works for jewellers.

 See e-invoicing in Jwero 

 Accounts and GST · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## Who must e-invoice

 E-invoicing applies to B2B invoices (and exports and credit or debit notes to businesses) for registered businesses whose aggregate turnover in any financial year from 2017-18 has been above ₹5 crore . For a jeweller, that usually means wholesalers, manufacturers and larger retailers who also sell to the trade.

 Check with your CA. Thresholds and reporting deadlines have changed several times. Confirm the current rules and whether they apply to you. Rules here are as we understand them in October 2026; tax and compliance rules change, and your CA’s reading of your business comes first.

## How it works

 You create the invoice in your billing software as usual. It is reported to the Invoice Registration Portal, which returns an IRN (Invoice Reference Number) and a signed QR code. The IRN and QR code go on the invoice you give the buyer. The details flow into your GSTR-1.

## The 30-day rule

 Businesses with turnover of ₹10 crore or more must report each invoice within 30 days of its date. A B2B invoice not reported in time cannot be reported later, which affects your buyer’s input credit.

## Retail bills are different

 Bills to individual customers (B2C) do not need an e-invoice. Only businesses above ₹500 crore turnover must show a dynamic QR code on B2C invoices.

## Where jewellers trip up

 A trade customer’s GSTIN missing or wrong on the bill.

 Approval goods billed late, outside the 30-day window.

 B2B and retail bills mixed in one series without the right tags.

# Girvi Business for Jewellers: Licence, Interest, Renewals and Auctions
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/girvi-gold-loan-business-guide

How a jeweller’s girvi (gold loan) business works: state licences and interest caps, how to calculate interest, renewals, release and auction notices.

GUIDE · GIRVI

## Running a girvi business

 Pledge, interest, renewal, release, and sometimes auction. The girvi cycle, the rules that govern it in most states, and the records that keep it out of trouble.

 See girvi in Jwero 

 Girvi and gold loans · 7 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## The girvi cycle

 Pledge: the customer leaves gold, you test and weigh it, and lend an amount against it.

 Interest: charged monthly on the loan.

 Renewal or part payment: the customer pays interest, or part of the loan, and the pledge continues.

 Release: the customer repays in full and takes the gold back.

 Default and auction: if the loan is not repaid, the gold is sold after the notice the law requires.

 Check with your lawyer. Girvi is regulated by state money-lending and pawnbroker laws: licences, interest caps, receipts and auction notice periods all differ by state. Rules here are as we understand them in October 2026, and they differ by state and change over time.

## Licence and interest caps

 Most states require a money-lender’s or pawnbroker’s licence for lending against gold, and cap the interest you can charge. The state act also sets what the pledge receipt must show and how long you must wait, and notify, before selling unredeemed gold.

## Valuing the pledge

 Test purity, weigh gross and net, and value the gold at today’s rate. Lend a share of that value, not all of it, so a fall in the gold rate does not leave the loan bigger than the gold. Write the gross weight, net weight, purity and value on the receipt.

## Calculating interest

 Most girvi interest is simple interest per month: loan × monthly rate × months . A ₹1,00,000 loan at 1.5% a month for 7 months is ₹10,500. Decide how part months are counted, and apply it the same way to every customer.

## Renewals and part payments

 When a customer pays only interest, record it and carry the pledge forward. When they pay part of the loan, reduce the principal from that date. Give a receipt each time; most girvi disputes are about payments the customer says they made.

## Release and auction

 On release, match the gold returned to the pledge record by weight in front of the customer. On default, send the notices your state requires, keep proof, and record the auction and how the proceeds were applied.

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero’s girvi module records pledges and loans, accrues interest, handles renewals, part payments and releases, prints the pledge receipt, and runs the default process with auction notices and auctions. Girvi reports show what is out, what is due and what is overdue. See ERP .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 Do jewellers need a licence for girvi? 
 In most states, lending against gold needs a money-lender’s or pawnbroker’s licence under the state’s money-lending law, which also caps interest and sets notice periods. Check your state’s act.

 How is girvi interest calculated? 
 Usually as simple interest per month on the loan amount: ₹1,00,000 at 1.5% a month is ₹1,500 a month. Use the method and the cap your state allows, and print it on the pledge receipt.

 How much can a jeweller lend against gold? 
 There is no single rule for jewellers. Many lend a share of today’s gold value to leave a margin if the rate falls; banks and NBFCs work to a 75% loan-to-value cap as a reference point.

 Can a jeweller auction unredeemed gold? 
 Only after the notice your state’s law requires, sent to the borrower in the prescribed way. Keep proof of every notice.

 Jwero runs pledges, interest, renewals, part payments, release and auction notices, with a receipt for each step.

# Karigar Wastage: Normal Loss, Caps and Settlement
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/karigar-wastage-norms-settlement

How much gold loss is normal at each stage, how to set wastage norms for karigars, cap recovery fairly, and settle every job in fine grams.

GUIDE · MANUFACTURING

## Karigar wastage: norms, caps and settlement

 Some gold is always lost in making. The question is how much is normal, who carries the rest, and whether you find out per job or at the year-end stock count.

 See karigar settlement in Jwero 

 Manufacturing · 6 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## Why loss is normal, and why it hides

 Filing, soldering, polishing and setting all lose some gold. Some comes back as dust and filings, some does not. When loss is only checked at the yearly stock count, a careful karigar and a careless one look the same.

## Set norms per process

 Take your own last few months of jobs and work out the loss per process: casting, filing, setting, polishing. That becomes the norm. Different designs can carry different norms; a heavy plain bangle is not a filigree necklace.

## Issue and receive in fine grams

 Fine weight = gross weight × purity. 50 g of 22K issued is 45.8 g fine. If the karigar returns 48 g of 22K finished work and 1.2 g of 22K scrap, that is 45.0 g fine back. The loss is 0.8 g fine, or 1.7%. Compare that to the norm.

## Cap recovery fairly

 A common rule: loss within the norm is the workshop’s cost; loss above the norm is recovered from the karigar, up to a cap. Write the norm and the cap on the job card before work starts, and settle each job when it comes back, not in a lump at month end.

## Read the pattern, not one job

 One high-loss job is noise. The same karigar above norm on most jobs is a conversation. The gold-loss calculator shows what loss above norm is worth over a year.

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero issues and receives karigar jobs by weight and purity, assesses wastage at settlement, and caps recovery to the norm you set. A karigar scorecard and metal reconciliation show loss by karigar over time. See manufacturing .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 What is a normal wastage percentage? 
 It depends on the process and design: filing and polishing lose less than intricate handmade work, and casting has its own losses. Set a norm per process from your own history, not a market number.

 Should karigars pay for loss above the norm? 
 Many workshops recover loss above an agreed norm, up to a cap. Put the norm and the cap in writing before the job is issued.

 Why settle in fine grams? 
 Because gold is issued and returned in different purities. Converting everything to fine (pure) gold is the only way the issue and the return can be compared fairly.

## Settle every job against its norm.

 Jwero assesses wastage per job and caps recovery to the norm you set, in fine grams.

# Fine-Weight Metal Ledger: Tracking Gold by Purity, Not Just Rupees
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/fine-weight-metal-ledger-jewellers

Why jewellers need a metal ledger in fine grams next to the money ledger, how to convert purities, and how it catches loss and mismatches early.

GUIDE · MANUFACTURING

## The fine-weight metal ledger

 Your books say what the gold cost. A metal ledger says where the gold is. Without it, loss, karigar balances and metal loans live in someone’s head.

 See the metal ledger in Jwero 

 Manufacturing · 6 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## Two ledgers, one business

 The money ledger records rupees. The metal ledger records grams of fine gold: what you bought, what you issued, what came back, what you sold. They should tell the same story. When they do not, something is missing.

## Converting to fine

 Fine weight = gross weight × purity. 22K is 91.6%, 18K is 75%, 14K is 58.5%. Record every movement in fine grams, along with the gross weight and purity it came from.

## What the ledger shows that the books do not

 Karigar balances: grams issued minus grams returned, per karigar.

 Metal loans: gold borrowed from or lent to suppliers, owed back in grams.

 Process loss: where in production the grams go.

 Stock in fine: total gold on hand, whatever the mix of purities.

## Reconcile every month

 Fine gold opening + purchases + returns from karigars − issues − sales should equal fine gold closing. A gap within your loss norms is normal. A gap outside them needs finding this month, not at the year end. See karigar wastage .

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero keeps a fine-weight metal ledger in the accounts, reconciles karigar metal issues and receipts, and records metal loans. See manufacturing and finance .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 What is fine weight? 
 The weight of pure gold in a piece: gross weight × purity. 10 g of 22K (91.6%) is 9.16 g fine.

 Why is a rupee ledger not enough? 
 Because the gold rate changes. A rupee balance cannot tell you whether a karigar owes you grams, and stock valued at different rates cannot be compared. Fine grams do not change with the rate.

 Who needs a metal ledger? 
 Anyone who issues gold to others: manufacturers, wholesalers who give metal to karigars, and retailers with in-house workshops or metal loans.

## Gold accounted for in grams and rupees.

 Jwero keeps a fine-weight metal ledger alongside the books, with karigar balances and metal loans on it.

# Job Work in Jewellery: Issue, Receipt, Challans and GST Rules
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/job-work-jewellery-gst-challan

Sending gold to karigars and job-work units: delivery challans, the one-year return rule, ITC-04, job-work GST, and keeping issue and receipt in fine grams.

GUIDE · MANUFACTURING

## Job work in jewellery

 Gold goes out on a challan and must come back, as jewellery or scrap, within the time the rules allow. Here is how issue, receipt and the paperwork fit together.

 See job work in Jwero 

 Manufacturing · 6 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## Issue on a challan

 When you send gold to a karigar or job-work unit, it is still yours. It moves on a delivery challan showing the item, gross weight, purity and fine weight. No GST is charged on the gold.

 Check with your CA. Job-work GST rules, the return period for ITC-04 and the deemed-supply timelines are the parts to confirm. Rules here are as we understand them in October 2026, and they differ by state and change over time.

## Receive against the challan

 What comes back is finished jewellery and scrap. Weigh both, convert to fine, and compare with what was issued. The difference is the loss, to be checked against your wastage norms .

## The time limit

 Under Section 143 of the CGST Act, inputs sent for job work should return within one year (capital goods within three). Gold not back in time is treated as supplied on the day it went out, with tax due. Track due dates per challan.

## The karigar’s bill

 A registered karigar bills you for making as a job-work service. An unregistered karigar does not charge GST. Either way, the making charge is your cost, separate from the gold.

## Reporting

 Goods sent to and received from job workers are reported in ITC-04. At the time of writing it is half-yearly if your turnover is above ₹5 crore and yearly otherwise.

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero issues job work to karigars and receives it back by weight and purity, sweeps for jobs that are due, settles wastage, and reconciles karigar metal. See manufacturing .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 Do I need to charge GST when sending gold to a karigar? 
 No. Sending your own gold for job work is not a sale. It moves on a delivery challan. The karigar’s making charge, if they are registered, is a job-work service billed to you.

 How long can gold stay with a job worker? 
 Under the GST rules, inputs sent for job work should come back within one year (capital goods three years). If not, the gold is treated as supplied on the day it was sent.

 What is ITC-04? 
 The return that reports goods sent to and received back from job workers. At the time of writing it is half-yearly above ₹5 crore turnover and yearly below. Confirm with your CA.

 Jwero issues and receives job work by weight and purity and flags jobs that are due back.

# Approval and Memo Stock: How Wholesalers Stop Losing Pieces on Approval
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/approval-memo-stock-jewellery-wholesale

Goods on approval are the easiest stock to lose track of. How to issue memos, set return dates, convert to sale and reconcile what came back.

GUIDE · WHOLESALE

## Approval and memo stock

 A retailer takes twenty pieces on approval, keeps four, returns twelve, and four are still somewhere. Memo stock is where wholesale margin quietly disappears.

 See approval memos in Jwero 

 Wholesale and trade · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## Why memo stock goes missing

 Pieces issued on a handwritten memo that is never closed.

 Partial returns written on the original slip.

 Kept pieces billed weeks later, at a different rate, or not at all.

## Issue properly

 List every piece with tag number, gross and net weight, purity and value. Set a return date. Give the buyer a copy and keep one. The memo travels as the document for the goods; it is not a sale.

## Close every memo

 Each memo ends in one of three ways for every piece: returned, billed, or chased. Issued pieces = returned + billed. Anything else is outstanding.

## Bill what is kept, at the agreed rate

 Agree up front whether kept pieces are billed at the rate on the issue date or the rate on the day of sale. Write it on the memo.

## Review the open memos weekly

 A list of everything out on approval, by buyer and by age, is the most useful report a wholesaler can read. See also challans and e-way bills .

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero issues approval memos and memo issues, records consignments and dispatch, and shows what is out with each buyer. See inventory and wholesale .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 What document should go with goods on approval? 
 A memo or delivery challan listing each piece with weight and value. It is not a sale until the buyer keeps the goods; then you raise an invoice.

 How long should goods stay on approval? 
 Set a return date on every memo, usually days not weeks, and follow up the day it passes. Goods out for months are a hidden loan to the buyer.

 How do I find what is missing? 
 Reconcile each memo: issued = returned + billed. Anything left over is what to chase.

 Jwero issues approval memos, tracks what is out with whom, and converts kept pieces to a sale.

# Managing Loose Diamonds and Gemstones: Stone Records, Parcels and Certificates

How diamond traders and jewellers keep loose stones under control: one record per stone or parcel, certificates, where each stone went, and memo to buyers.

## Managing loose diamonds and gemstones

 A stone sheet in Excel works until a stone is mounted, sent on memo, or split from a parcel. Then nobody can say where it is or what it became.

## One record per stone, or per parcel

 Certified stones need their own record: shape, carat weight, colour, clarity, cut, certificate number and lab. Melee and small stones are tracked as parcels, by total weight and count, with sizes.

 A stone moves: from a parcel, onto a memo, into a setting, back for re-setting. Each move should be recorded against the stone, so you can always answer where it is and what it became.

 Price certified stones per carat by their grades; price parcels by weight. Keep cost and selling price on the record so margin is visible per stone. See the price guide for how stones sit on a jewellery bill.

## Memo to buyers

 Stones on approval are easy to lose. Issue them on a memo , stone by stone.

A: Link the stone record to the piece it went into. Then the jewellery carries its stones, and returns or re-sets can be traced.

Q: What about stones sent on memo?
A: Issue them on a memo with each stone listed, and close the memo when they come back or are billed.

# Jewellery Repairs: Job Slips, Turnaround Times and Who Holds the Piece
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/jewellery-repair-job-slip-tat

Run jewellery repairs without lost pieces or angry customers: a proper job slip, weights in and out, turnaround promises, ready alerts and warranty.

GUIDE · SERVICE

## Jewellery repairs: job slips and turnaround

 A repair is a customer’s piece in your custody. The job slip, the weights and the date you promised are what protect both of you.

 See repairs in Jwero 

 Counter · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## The job slip

 At drop-off, record: customer name and phone, a description and a photo, gross weight, the work to be done, the estimate, and the promised date. Give the customer a copy. Most repair disputes come down to what was written at this moment.

## Weigh in, weigh out

 Weigh the piece in front of the customer when it comes in and when it goes out. If gold is added or removed by the work, write it on the slip.

## Promise a date, and keep it

 Set a turnaround per type of work: a clasp in two days, a re-polish in a week. Track how many repairs are past their date. Customers forgive a delay they are told about; not one they discover.

## Tell them when it is ready

 A message the day the piece is ready brings customers back, and a returning customer often buys. A list of ready pieces waiting more than a week tells you who to call.

## Warranty

 If you offer a warranty on repairs, write its terms on the slip, and record which repairs are under it. Our custody chain guide covers keeping track of a piece while it is with you.

# Gold Scheme Accounting: Why Instalments Are a Liability, Not Sales
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/gold-scheme-accounting-liability

How to account for gold savings scheme instalments: advances held as a liability until redemption, bonuses, closures, and reconciling members to the books.

GUIDE · GOLD SCHEMES

## Gold scheme accounting

 Scheme money is the customer’s, held against a future purchase. Booking it as sales flatters this month and creates a hole on redemption day.

 See gold schemes in Jwero 

 Gold schemes · 6 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## Whose money is it?

 A scheme instalment is the customer’s money, paid in advance against jewellery they will buy later. Until they redeem, you owe it to them, as jewellery or, in some cases, as a refund. That makes it a liability, not a sale.

 Check with your CA. The accounting and GST treatment of scheme advances and bonuses, and any limits under company deposit rules, should be confirmed for your business. Rules here are as we understand them in October 2026, and they differ by state and change over time.

## Why it matters

 Booking instalments as sales makes months look better than they were.

 On redemption, the jewellery goes out with no money coming in, and the margin looks like a loss.

 You cannot tell at any moment how much you owe your members.

## The flow

 Instalment received: cash or bank up, scheme liability up.

 Maturity: the bonus is added to what the member can redeem.

 Redemption: the sale is recorded; the liability comes off against it.

## Reconcile members to the books

 Total of every member’s balance = scheme liability in the accounts. Check it every month. A gap means an instalment recorded in one place and not the other.

## Structure matters too

 Many schemes run for 11 or 12 months, partly because of how deposit rules treat advances that are not used within a year. Read are gold savings schemes legal and talk to your advisor about yours.

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero records scheme instalments against each member, accounts for them as a liability, closes schemes into a sale, and reports what you owe members. See gold schemes .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 Are scheme instalments income? 
 No. They are advances from customers against a future purchase, and sit as a liability until the member redeems. The sale is recognised when the jewellery is bought.

 How is the bonus instalment accounted for? 
 The bonus your shop adds at maturity is usually a discount on the sale at redemption, not a cost when each instalment arrives. Confirm the treatment with your CA.

 Is GST charged on instalments? 
 The treatment of advances for goods under GST has changed over time. Ask your CA how instalments and the final sale should be taxed in your case.

## Your scheme book and your accounts, matching.

 Jwero accounts for scheme money as a liability and shows what you owe members at any moment.

# 11+1 Gold Scheme vs Gram Accumulation: Which Suits Your Shop?
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/gold-scheme-types-11-plus-1-vs-grams

The two common gold savings schemes compared: fixed monthly instalments with a bonus, or buying grams at each instalment. Who each suits, and the risks.

GUIDE · GOLD SCHEMES

## 11+1 schemes vs gram accumulation

 Pay eleven, get one free. Or buy a few grams every month at that day’s rate. Same goal, very different risk for you and value for the customer.

 See gold schemes in Jwero 

 Gold schemes · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## The 11+1 instalment scheme

 The customer pays, say, ₹5,000 a month for 11 months: ₹55,000. At maturity the shop adds a bonus, often ₹5,000, and the customer redeems ₹60,000 against jewellery at that day’s rate.

 For you: simple, and the bonus is a known cost, usually recovered in the making on the piece.

 For the customer: easy to understand, but if gold rises, their rupees buy less gold.

## Gram accumulation

 Each instalment buys gold at that day’s rate. ₹5,000 at ₹6,875 a gram buys 0.727 g. Over a year the customer accumulates grams, and redeems the grams, often with a making-charge benefit.

 For you: you owe grams, not rupees, so a rate rise raises what you owe. Hedge or hold stock against it.

 For the customer: protected from rate rises, and averages their buying price.

## Which to offer

 Many shops offer both: instalment schemes for customers who think in rupees, gram schemes for those who think in gold. Whatever you run, account for it as a liability (see scheme accounting ), and write the terms down.

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero supports traditional instalment plans and gram-accumulation plans, with OTP enrolment, autodebit mandates, reminders, a passbook sent on WhatsApp, and closure into a sale. Old gold can also be put into a scheme. See gold schemes and the scheme calculator .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 What is an 11+1 gold scheme? 
 The customer pays a fixed amount each month for 11 months, and the shop adds a bonus, often equal to one instalment, at maturity. The total is redeemed against jewellery.

 What is a gram accumulation scheme? 
 Each instalment buys gold at that day’s rate, and the customer accumulates grams. At maturity they redeem the grams, usually without paying making on part or all of them.

 Which is better for the jeweller? 
 Instalment schemes are simpler and the cost of the bonus is known. Gram schemes protect the customer from rate rises, so the shop carries more of that risk.

## Run either scheme, or both.

 Jwero supports instalment and gram-accumulation plans, with a passbook on WhatsApp.

# Stock Transfers Between Jewellery Branches: Challans, GST and Control
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/branch-stock-transfer-jewellery

Moving stock between showrooms without losing track: transfer documents, GST on inter-state transfers, approvals, and reconciling what was sent and received.

GUIDE · CHAINS

## Stock transfers between branches

 Stock leaves one showroom and should arrive at another. In between it is nobody’s, unless every transfer is sent, received and checked piece by piece.

 See transfers in Jwero 

 Multi-store · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## Within your state

 Stock moving between branches under the same GSTIN moves on a delivery challan, without GST. List every piece with tag, weight and value.

 Check with your CA. Inter-state transfers between your own branches are taxable supplies. Confirm the valuation and paperwork for your setup. Rules here are as we understand them in October 2026, and they differ by state and change over time.

## Between states

 Branches in different states have different GSTINs, and GST treats them as separate persons. A transfer between them is billed with GST, and the receiving branch claims it as input credit.

## Control

 Approval by someone other than the sender.

 Scan each tag out, and scan it in at the other end.

 A list of transfers sent but not received, by age.

## Vaults and locker moves

 The same discipline applies to moves between the showroom floor and the vault at night. If it is not recorded, the morning count will not match.

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero records stock transfers between branches and vaults, so every move has a sending and a receiving record. See multi-store and chains .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 Is GST charged on transfers between branches? 
 Within the same state, a transfer moves on a delivery challan without GST. Between states, branches with different GSTINs are treated as separate persons, so the transfer is billed with GST. Confirm with your CA.

 Who should approve a transfer? 
 Someone other than the person sending it, usually a manager at either end, so no single person can move stock alone.

 How do I catch a missing piece? 
 Receive every transfer by scanning each tag at the receiving branch. Sent minus received should be zero.

 Jwero moves stock between branches and vaults with a record at both ends.

# Jewellery Exhibitions: Taking Stock Out and Bringing It Back
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/jewellery-exhibition-stock-control

How to run a jewellery exhibition or trunk show without stock gaps: issue lists, sales at the venue, GST registration in another state, and counting everything back.

GUIDE · CHAINS

## Running a jewellery exhibition

 Hundreds of pieces leave the showroom for three days. Most sell or come back. The ones that do neither are what an exhibition really costs, if you do not count properly.

 See exhibitions in Jwero 

 Multi-store · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## Before you go

 List every piece going out, with tag, weight and value, on a delivery challan. Insure the stock for transit and the venue. If the exhibition is in another state, register as a casual taxable person before the event.

 Check with your CA. Casual taxable person registration, advance tax deposit and returns for out-of-state exhibitions. Rules here are as we understand them in October 2026, and they differ by state and change over time.

## At the venue

 Bill every sale on the spot, against the piece’s own tag, so the sale and the stock move together. Trials and holds should be recorded too: a piece taken to a customer’s hotel room is still yours.

## Coming back

 Scan every piece back in the day you return. Issued = sold + returned. Follow up any difference the same week.

## Afterwards

 Exhibition visitors who asked but did not buy are your best leads for the next month. Record who they were and what they looked at.

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero records exhibition stock and trials, bills at the venue against tagged pieces, and shows what is still out. See inventory .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

 Do I need GST registration to sell at an exhibition in another state? 
 Usually yes, as a casual taxable person, registered before the event, with an advance deposit of the estimated tax. Confirm with your CA.

 What document goes with exhibition stock? 
 A delivery challan listing every piece, since moving stock to an exhibition is not a sale.

 How do I count stock back after an exhibition? 
 Scan every piece back in on return. Issued = sold + returned. Investigate any difference before the next event.

# Custom Jewellery Orders: From Enquiry to Delivery Without Delays
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/custom-jewellery-order-process

How to run custom and made-to-order jewellery: taking the order, advances and rate booking, sending it to the karigar, tracking due dates and delivering on time.

GUIDE · ORDERS

## Custom jewellery orders

 A bride’s set promised for the 14th. An advance taken, a rate booked, a karigar briefed. Custom orders fail in the gaps between those steps.

 See orders in Jwero 

 Counter · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## Taking the order

 Record the design, purity, approximate weight, stones, size, the customer’s date, and the price basis. Attach the design image or sketch. Give the customer a copy with the order number.

## Advance and rate

 Take an advance and record the rate policy: is the rate fixed on the day of the advance, or set on delivery? Customers argue about this more than anything else in custom orders. Write it down.

## To the karigar

 Issue the job with the metal by weight and purity, and a due date a few days before the customer’s. See job work .

## Track due dates daily

 One list of every open custom order, its karigar and its due date, reviewed every morning, prevents most late deliveries.

## Delivery

 Weigh the finished piece, price it on the basis agreed, adjust the advance, and bill. Tell the customer the day it is ready.

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero records customer orders and quotations (with a link the customer can open), issues the work to karigars by weight, and sweeps for jobs that are due. See manufacturing and bridal .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 Should I book the gold rate on a custom order? 
 Decide your policy and write it on the order: either the rate on the day of the advance is fixed for the gold the advance covers, or the final rate applies on delivery.

 How much advance should I take? 
 Enough to cover your risk if the customer does not collect: many shops take a share of the estimated value, or the value of the gold.

 How do I stop orders running late? 
 Give every order a due date at the karigar a few days before the customer’s date, and review overdue jobs daily.

# Birthday and Anniversary Marketing for Jewellers, Done Automatically
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/birthday-anniversary-marketing-jewellers

Occasions are the best reason a customer has to buy jewellery. How to collect dates, plan the message, reach the whole family, and run it without a team.

GUIDE · CUSTOMERS

## Birthday and anniversary marketing

 Every customer has dates that call for jewellery. Most shops collect them on the bill and never use them. Here is how to turn them into visits, every month, without anyone remembering.

 See occasion journeys in Jwero 

 Customers · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## Why occasions work

 A birthday or anniversary is the most common reason to buy jewellery that is not a wedding. The customer already plans to spend; the only question is where. The shop that reminds them early, by name, usually wins.

## Collect dates as a habit

 At billing: birthday and anniversary on every customer record.

 On scheme enrolment: the reason they are saving, and when.

 From the family: the spouse’s birthday, children’s birthdays. One household can mean five or six occasions a year.

## Plan the timing

 Three weeks before an anniversary: a suggestion, with pieces in their range.

 Ten days before a birthday: a reminder to the person who buys, not only the person celebrating.

 On the day: a greeting, nothing to sell.

## Make it personal

 Use their name, what they bought last time, and the price range they usually buy in. “Your anniversary is on the 14th. Last year you chose earrings; here are three new pendant sets in the same style” beats any festive broadcast.

## Ask before you send

 Only message customers who agreed to hear from you, and make it easy to stop. See WhatsApp for jewellers .

 How do I collect occasion dates? 
 At billing, on the scheme form, and when a customer replies on WhatsApp. Ask for the spouse’s and children’s dates too: a family is several occasions a year.

 Will customers find it intrusive? 
 Not if they agreed to hear from you, the message is personal, and it comes a few times a year, not every week.

# AI Phone Calls for Jewellers: Scheme Reminders, Follow-Ups and Missed Calls
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/ai-calling-jewellers-scheme-reminders

Where AI calling helps a jewellery business: scheme instalment reminders, enquiry follow-ups and missed calls, with a person approving what matters, and the rules to respect.

GUIDE · AI

## AI phone calls for jewellers

 Hundreds of scheme reminders a month, follow-ups after every enquiry, calls missed in the rush. The routine calls an AI can make, and the ones a person should.

 See AI calling in Jwero 

 AI · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## The calls nobody has time for

 A shop with 500 scheme members makes or misses 500 reminder calls a month. Add follow-ups on every enquiry and calls back for missed calls in the evening rush, and it is a full-time job nobody is doing.

 Check with your advisor. TRAI rules on commercial communication, registration for promotional calls, and consent records. Rules here are as we understand them in October 2026.

## Where AI calling fits

 Scheme reminders a few days before the instalment is due.

 Ready for collection for repairs and custom orders.

 Appointment confirmations the day before.

 First follow-up after an enquiry, to book a visit.

## Where a person takes over

 Complaints, large purchases, negotiation, and any customer who asks for a person. A good setup hands the call, with what was said, to the right salesperson.

## In the customer’s language

 Calls work best in the language the customer speaks at home. See selling in regional languages .

## Measure it

 Track instalments collected on time, visits booked, and calls handed to staff. If on-time instalments rise, the calls are paying for themselves.

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero’s voice agent places and answers calls through a telephony provider, with speech recognition and voice in Indian languages, and records what was said on the customer’s record. See AI calling and gold schemes .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 Which calls should an AI make? 
 Routine, predictable ones: scheme instalment reminders, ready-for-collection calls, appointment confirmations and first follow-ups after an enquiry.

 Which calls should a person make? 
 Anything involving a complaint, a large purchase, a negotiation or a customer who asks for a person. The AI should hand over, not hold on.

 Are there rules for automated calls? 
 Yes. Promotional calls in India are regulated by TRAI, and customers must be able to opt out. Service calls to existing customers are treated differently. Confirm your setup before calling at scale.

 Jwero’s voice agent handles reminders and follow-ups in Indian languages, under the rules you set.

# Counting Showroom Footfall and Conversion for Jewellers
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/jewellery-showroom-footfall-conversion

How many people walked in, and how many bought? How to count footfall, measure walk-in conversion by counter and hour, and act on it, with privacy in mind.

GUIDE · CHAINS

## Showroom footfall and conversion

 Sales tells you who bought. It says nothing about the thirty people who walked in and left. Footfall is the other half of the number.

 See footfall counting in Jwero 

 Retail operations · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## The number you are missing

 If 200 people walk in on a Saturday and 20 buy, conversion is 10%. If you only see the 20 bills, you cannot tell whether Saturday was busy and badly served, or quiet and well served.

 Check with your advisor. Camera notices, data retention and India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act. Rules here are as we understand them in October 2026.

## What to measure

 Footfall by hour and by day.

 Conversion = bills ÷ footfall, by branch and hour.

 Average bill , to see whether busy hours rush customers into smaller purchases.

## What it changes

 Staffing: put your best salespeople on the hours with high footfall and low conversion.

 Marketing: see whether a campaign brought people in, not only sales.

 Branches: compare like for like, not just total sales.

## Do not lose the walk-outs

 The customer who leaves without buying is still a lead. Capture a number at the counter and follow up. See tracking walk-ins .

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero connects showroom cameras to count footfall and follow the customer’s path in the showroom, and sets it against sales. See footfall counting .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 What is a good walk-in conversion rate for a jewellery shop? 
 It varies by city, season and price range, so compare yourself with yourself: by branch, by day and by hour. A rise after a change tells you it worked.

 How is footfall counted? 
 Usually with cameras at the entrance that count people coming in. Staff counting by hand misses people in the rush.

 Do I need to tell customers about cameras? 
 Yes. Display clear notices, keep footage only as long as needed, and follow India’s data protection law. Take advice on your setup.

## Know who walked in, not just who bought.

 Jwero counts showroom footfall from cameras and sets it against sales, by hour and branch.

# Selling Gold Jewellery Online at the Live Rate: Shopify, WooCommerce and Marketplaces
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/selling-gold-jewellery-online-live-rate

Online gold prices go stale every time the rate moves. How to price by weight and purity online, keep Shopify or WooCommerce in step with the counter, and avoid selling at yesterday’s rate.

GUIDE · ONLINE

## Selling gold jewellery online at the live rate

 A fixed price on a gold piece is wrong by the next morning. Online, that means selling below cost on a rising day and losing the sale on a falling one.

 See the storefront in Jwero 

 Online · 6 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## The problem with fixed prices

 A 10 gram 22K chain priced when gold was ₹6,875 a gram is ₹1,000 or more out within days if the rate moves. On a rising day you sell below what you should; on a falling day the customer finds it cheaper elsewhere.

## Price online the way you price at the counter

 Store each product’s net weight, purity, making and stones, and calculate the price from today’s rate, exactly as on the bill. See the price formula and calculator .

## Keep the store in step

 When the rate changes, every product price should be recalculated and pushed to the store. Doing it by hand for hundreds of products is how stale prices happen.

## One stock

 A piece shown online is also in the showroom. Sell it in one place and it must disappear from the other, or it will be sold twice.

## Product details buyers need

 Weight, purity, hallmark, stone details and a price breakdown. Online buyers cannot hold the piece; detail is what builds trust.

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero prices products from rate, purity, weight and making, recalculates on a schedule when rates change, and syncs with Shopify and WooCommerce, mapping metal and stone details into the store. It also runs its own storefront. See storefront and Jwero vs Shopify .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 Can Shopify price jewellery by gold rate? 
 Not on its own; Shopify stores a fixed price. You need a tool that recalculates prices from weight, purity and the rate and updates the store when the rate changes.

 How often should online prices update? 
 Every time you change your rate, usually once or twice a day. Updating less often means the website and the counter disagree.

 What about marketplaces? 
 Marketplaces need the same discipline: prices that follow the rate, and stock that matches the shop, so a piece is not sold twice.

## The same price online and at the counter.

 Jwero prices every piece from today’s rate and keeps your store in step when it moves.

# Jewellery Staff Incentives: Setting Targets Salespeople Trust
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/jewellery-staff-incentives-targets

How to design sales incentives for jewellery staff: what to reward, gold vs diamond targets, team vs individual, and paying on numbers everyone can see.

GUIDE · TEAM

## Staff incentives and targets

 Incentives work when staff believe the number. They backfire when the calculation is a spreadsheet only the owner understands.

 See incentives in Jwero 

 Team · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## Reward what you want more of

 Making charges or margin , not gold value, which moves with the rate.

 Diamond and studded sales , where skill makes the difference.

 Scheme enrolments and repeat customers , which build next year.

## Individual and team

 Pure individual targets make staff fight over the customer at the door. A team share for the showroom’s total, plus an individual share, keeps both effort and cooperation.

## Credit the right person

 Record the salesperson on every bill, and decide in advance how shared sales split. Disputes about who sold what kill more incentive schemes than the amounts.

## Show the number daily

 Each salesperson should see where they stand today, not discover it on payday.

## Keep it simple

 If a salesperson cannot work out their own incentive, it will not motivate them. Two or three measures, written down, is enough. See also sales staff management .

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero records the salesperson on each bill, tracks targets and scorecards, and works out incentives in payroll from the same numbers. See staff management .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 Should incentives be on sales value or margin? 
 Gold sales value rises and falls with the rate, so many shops reward on making charges, diamond and studded sales, or weight sold, which reflect effort rather than the market.

 Individual or team incentives? 
 A mix works best: an individual share for what each person sells, and a team share so nobody fights over walk-ins.

 How often should incentives be paid? 
 Monthly, with a daily view of progress. A target seen only at month end does not change behaviour.

## Targets your team can see every day.

 Jwero tracks sales by salesperson against targets and works out incentives from the same numbers.

For jewellery franchise networks: what to keep central (brand, pricing, catalogue, schemes), what to leave to partners, and the reports a franchisor needs.

## Running a jewellery franchise

 A franchise network sells one brand through many owners. Get the split of control wrong and you get either inconsistent stores or unhappy partners.

 See Jwero for franchise networks 

 Franchise · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## Keep central

 Catalogue and pricing rules: the same piece should not cost different amounts in two stores of the same brand.

 Scheme terms: a customer who enrols in one store should be able to redeem as promised.

 Brand and customer standards. 

## Leave to the partner

 Hiring and managing their team.

 Local events and marketing, within brand rules.

 Day-to-day running of the store.

## Exceptions with approval

 Partners will want local price exceptions, discounts and special orders. Allow them through an approval, so the exception is visible rather than hidden.

## The franchisor’s view

 Sales, stock, ageing and scheme collections by store, from the same system the stores use. Monthly spreadsheets sent in by partners arrive late and never quite match.

 Brand, catalogue, pricing rules, scheme terms and customer experience standards. These are what customers expect to be the same in every store.

 What should franchise partners control? 
 Their own staff, local marketing within brand rules, and day-to-day operations of their store.

 What reports does a franchisor need? 
 Sales, stock and ageing by store, scheme collections, and customer complaints, ideally from the same system rather than monthly spreadsheets.

 Jwero runs central pricing and catalogue with each partner’s own store on the same system.

# Silver Jewellery Business: Pricing, Making, Wastage and Margins
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/silver-jewellery-business-pricing

How silver jewellery is priced in India: rate per gram or kg, purity, making per gram or piece, touch and wastage, GST, and where silver margins are made.

GUIDE · SILVER

## The silver jewellery business

 Silver moves fast, sells by the piece as often as by weight, and has thinner metal value, so making and design carry the margin.

 See Jwero for silver retail 

 Pricing · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## The formula

 Price = silver rate per gram × purity × net weight + making + GST at 3% 

 Silver rates are often quoted per kilogram; divide by 1,000 for the per-gram rate. Example: ₹90,000 a kg is ₹90 a gram. A 50 g sterling (92.5%) anklet pair: 50 × ₹90 × 0.925 = ₹4,163 metal.

 Check with your advisor. Silver hallmarking status and purity grades with BIS. Rules here are as we understand them in October 2026.

## Making carries the margin

 Because the metal value is low, making is often the larger part of the price: per gram for heavier pieces, per piece for light items, or a percentage for designer work. Some shops charge “touch” and wastage instead, expressed in purity or weight.

## Fixed prices for light pieces

 Toe rings, light earrings and gift items sell better at a round fixed price. Review those prices when the rate moves a lot, or the margin quietly disappears.

## Stock moves fast

 Silver ranges are wide and pieces are small. Tagging each piece and watching what does not move is what keeps silver profitable. See dead stock .

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero prices silver the same way as gold, from rate, purity, weight and making, or at a fixed price per piece, with tags and stock ageing. See silver retail .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 How is silver jewellery priced? 
 Like gold: rate per gram × purity × net weight, plus making, plus 3% GST. Many light silver items are instead sold at a fixed price per piece.

 What purity is silver jewellery? 
 Sterling silver is 92.5%. Other common purities are used for traditional and heavier silver. State the purity on the bill.

 Is silver hallmarking mandatory? 
 At the time of writing, silver hallmarking is voluntary in India. Check the current position with BIS.

## Silver priced right, piece by piece.

 Jwero prices silver from the rate, purity and weight, or as a fixed price per piece, and keeps the catalogue in step.

# Lab-Grown Diamonds: Pricing, Disclosure and Selling Them Next to Natural
URL: https://jwero.ai/blog/lab-grown-diamond-jewellery-selling

How jewellers can sell lab-grown diamonds honestly: clear disclosure on tags and bills, certificates, pricing per carat, and keeping natural and lab-grown stock apart.

GUIDE · DIAMONDS

## Selling lab-grown diamonds

 Lab-grown diamonds open a price point many customers could not reach. They also need clear disclosure, separate stock and pricing that holds up when prices keep falling.

 See Jwero for lab-grown jewellers 

 Diamonds and stones · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published October 2026 

## Disclose clearly, every time

 Say “laboratory-grown diamond” on the tag, the display, the bill and the certificate. Customers who choose lab-grown knowingly are happy customers; customers who find out later are complaints.

 Check with your advisor. Disclosure wording, consumer protection rules and the GST rate on loose lab-grown stones. Rules here are as we understand them in October 2026.

## Keep the stock apart

 Natural and lab-grown stones look the same to the eye. Keep them as different stone types in your records, in different parcels, and never on the same memo without labels.

## Certificates

 Record the lab and certificate number on each certified stone. Buyers increasingly check.

## Pricing

 Price per carat by grade, as with natural. Lab-grown prices have fallen fast; review them often, and be careful with stock bought at older prices. See managing loose stones .

## Selling next to natural

 Many customers compare. Show the two side by side with clear labels and let the customer choose: size and design with lab-grown, rarity and long-term value with natural.

## How Jwero does it

 Jwero keeps a stone master and individual stone records with certificate details, follows each stone into the piece it is set in, and prints what the record says on tags and bills. See lab-grown diamond jewellers .

 GUIDE QUESTIONS

## What jewellers ask about this.

 Do I have to tell customers a diamond is lab-grown? 
 Yes. Describe it clearly as laboratory-grown on the tag, the bill and the certificate. Calling it just “diamond” is misleading and risks consumer complaints.

 Are lab-grown diamonds certified? 
 Yes, by major gemological labs, with reports that state the stone is laboratory-grown. Keep the certificate number on the stone record.

 How should lab-grown diamonds be priced? 
 Per carat by grade, like natural, but expect wholesale prices to keep changing. Review prices more often than for natural stones.

## Natural and lab-grown, never mixed up.

 Jwero records each stone with its type and certificate, so tags and bills say exactly what it is.

# Owner / Proprietor, Run the Shop From a Record You Own
URL: https://jwero.ai/roles/owner

How Jwero changes the owner’s day: today’s sales, cash and stock on one screen, enquiries answered while you sleep, and a record owned by the shop, not one person’s head.

LEADERSHIP · OWNER

## You built this business on memory. Now it has a backup.

 Right now, if you’re not in the shop, half the context leaves with you, who’s due a call, what’s ageing on the shelf, what the vendor is owed, how the day closed. Jwero puts all of it on a record the business owns, shows you today’s sales, cash, stock and pending work on one screen, and has a governed AI workforce handle the repetitive parts while you keep every real decision.

 Book a demo 

 A DAY IN THIS ROLE

## What actually changes between opening and closing.

 Today With Jwero 

 An enquiry at 9pm 

 Today A WhatsApp message sits unanswered overnight, the customer has already messaged two other jewellers by morning.

 With Jwero The AI workforce drafts a priced reply from the live catalogue within minutes; if it’s within your rules it can send under your daily caps, or wait for your morning approval.

 Knowing who to follow up with 

 Today You remember the regulars, but the customer whose scheme matured last month, or who mentioned a wedding six months out, is easy to lose track of.

 With Jwero The customer record surfaces who’s due, scheme maturities, occasions, RFM signals, as a drafted follow-up waiting in your approval queue, not a fact you had to recall.

 Checking on the business from outside the shop See WhatsApp Commerce → 

 Today You call the manager, or wait until you’re physically back at the counter, to know what happened today.

 With Jwero A weekly plain-language report and a live view of the customer, stock and billing picture, reachable without a phone call to the store.

 Pricing at the live gold rate See Billing & Finance → 

 Today Someone recalculates prices by hand when the rate moves, and mistakes creep into invoices.

 With Jwero Catalogue and billing prices resolve from the live rate automatically; any manual override routes through an approval so nothing slips past you.

 Knowing who walked out without buying See Showroom Intelligence → 

 Today A customer tries on three pieces, leaves without a word, and by the time you hear about it from staff, if you ever do, the moment to follow up has passed.

 With Jwero The live floor view logs the visit and the pieces she was shown; Walkout Rescue drafts a WhatsApp follow-up naming them for a person to check and send, and it shows up in the daily brief when you look.

 WHAT THIS ROLE GAINS

## Skills that compound instead of living only in your head.

## Structured relationship management

 Instead of remembering which customers matter, you work from a record that scores every signal a customer gives, occasions, scheme balances, taste, RFM, 11 live scores, and shows you why, not just who.

## Data-backed decision making

 Dead-stock ageing, fast/slow movers and a weekly report replace gut calls with a number you can actually check.

## Delegated oversight, not delegated control

 Approval queues, daily caps and a 5-scope kill switch let you extend how the business responds to customers without handing away the final word.

## Cross-channel fluency

 One inbox for WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook means you stop needing to check four apps to know what customers are asking.

 SURVIVING & GROWING IN THE AI AGE

## AI drafts. You approve. That doesn’t change.

 What stays entirely yours: which customer relationship to protect, which price exception makes sense, which risk is worth taking. See why this is true for every role at Jwero → 

 HOW TO CONTRIBUTE MORE

## Concrete moves, not vague advice.

 1 

## Set your approval rhythm
 Decide how often you review the AI workforce’s approval queue, daily is enough for most stores, so drafted replies and follow-ups don’t stall waiting on you.

 2 

## Read the weekly report before the walk-through
 Use the plain-language weekly report to know what to ask your team, instead of discovering issues on the floor.

 3 

## Check dead-stock ageing monthly
 The ageing bands (0–30, 31–90, 91–180, 180+ days) tell you what capital is sitting idle before it becomes a write-off conversation.

 4 

## Tune the kill switch scopes to your comfort level
 Start conservative, one agent or one channel at a time, and widen what the AI workforce can do as you build trust in what it drafts.

 OWNER QUESTIONS

## Control, the billing counter, and what actually changes.

 I already carry the whole business in my head. Why do I need this? 
 Because your head is a single point of failure, a sick day, a family emergency or a second store means the memory doesn’t scale. Jwero puts the customer relationships, the stock truth and the pending decisions on a record the business owns, so the shop still runs the way you’d run it even when you’re not the one answering.

 Will I lose control of pricing and messaging if AI is drafting things? 
 No, every AI-drafted message, offer or price exception sits in an approval queue until you or someone you’ve authorised taps approve. Daily caps, quiet hours and a 5-scope kill switch mean you decide how much rope the AI staff get, and you can pull it back instantly.

 Does Jwero replace my billing counter? 
 Yes. Scan or search a piece, price it at the live gold rate, apply a discount, take old gold in exchange, generate the GST invoice; returns and a reconciled cash day-close are in the same counter. Your statutory books can still live in Tally through the bridge. See the Counter POS .

 What actually changes for me day to day? 
 Enquiries get answered on WhatsApp even after closing, follow-ups draft themselves instead of being forgotten, and you get a weekly plain-language report instead of reconstructing the picture from memory and a notebook.
