# Jewellery Manufacturing Software: A Buyer’s Guide
URL: https://jwero.ai/guides/jewellery-manufacturing-software

How jewellery manufacturing software controls gold on the workshop floor: orders, bills of materials, issue and return in fine weight, karigar accounts, wastage norms by stage, job work for clients, QC and hallmarking.

BUYER’S GUIDE

## Jewellery manufacturing software: karigar, wastage and job work

 In a workshop the product and the raw material are the same precious metal. This is how software keeps count of it from the order to the finished piece.

 See manufacturing in Jwero 
 See the price 

 Buyer’s guide · 12 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Reviewed October 2026 

## The one question every workshop must answer

 Gold goes in. Jewellery comes out. Is the difference what it should be? Everything in jewellery manufacturing software exists to answer that, for every job, every stage and every karigar, on the day it happens.

 Most workshops answer it at month end, from a register and a karigar’s khata book, when the gold is long gone and nobody can say where. Software moves the answer to the moment a job is returned.

## Fine weight: the language of the floor

 A workshop handles metal at different purities: fine gold, 22 karat, 18 karat, alloys, solder. Adding their gross weights is meaningless. Converting each to its pure gold content, the fine weight, gives one number that can be issued, returned and balanced. Any software for the floor must account in fine weight, and show gross weight and purity beside it.

## From order to dispatch

 Step What happens What must be recorded 
 Order A retailer or your own shop asks for pieces Design, quantity, purity, due date 
 Bill of materials What each piece needs Metal, stones, findings, expected weight 
 Routing The stages it will pass through Casting, filing, setting, polishing and so on 
 Issue Metal and stones go to a karigar or department Fine weight out, against a job 
 Return Work comes back Weight in, scrap, dust recovered 
 Loss check Issue minus return, compared with the norm Flag anything beyond the norm 
 Quality check Finish, weight, stone count Pass, rework or reject 
 Hallmarking Sent to the assaying centre HUID received against each piece 
 Finished goods The piece enters stock Final weights, cost from actuals 
 Dispatch and billing Delivered or sent on memo Invoice or memo, and the party ledger 

## Wastage norms, stage by stage

 Some loss is real: metal is filed away, lost in polishing, left in a crucible. Each stage has a loss that is normal for it. A norm is that expected loss, set by you for each stage and type of work. Software compares actual loss with the norm when the job is returned. Within the norm, nothing happens. Beyond it, somebody is told that day.

 The point is not to accuse anyone. It is to find the leak while it is still one job, not a month. The gold loss calculator shows what an unexplained gap costs at today’s rate, and the wastage control guide goes deeper.

## The karigar’s account

 A karigar holds your metal and is owed wages. The khata records both: metal issued, metal returned, the balance he holds, the work done and what he is to be paid. Disputes happen when the workshop’s register and the karigar’s memory differ.

 Good software gives both sides the same account. The karigar can see his own balance. Wages can be settled against gold where that is your practice. Nothing depends on who remembers loudest at settlement.

## Job work for other people’s gold

 Many units make for retailers and brands who supply the metal. That metal is not yours. It must be received, held, used and returned client by client, never mixed, with a statement each client can trust. Billing is for labour, on the weights actually produced. If you do job work, test this first: issue from one client’s metal and confirm it cannot be charged to another’s.

## Metal closure

 At the end of a period, opening metal plus receipts should equal issues, returns, finished goods, scrap, recorded loss and closing stock. If it does not close, something is unrecorded. Software should do this closure on demand, by department and by karigar, not once a year.

## Casting, handmade and machine-made

 Casting works in trees and flasks. Loss is measured per flask, and sprues and returns go back as scrap of known purity.

 Handmade work moves between individual karigars, each with a khata.

 Machine-made chain and stamped work runs in lots, with loss by lot and by machine stage.

 Most units mix all three. The routing should describe your floor, not force it into one pattern.

## Costing from what really happened

 A quoted price is built on an estimate: expected weight, expected loss, expected labour. The true cost is known only when the job is finished. Software should cost each piece from actual metal used, actual loss, stones set and wages paid, and show the gap between estimate and actual. Over a few months that gap tells you which designs and which customers are profitable, and which you have been making at a loss.

## Raw material, scrap and refining

 Metal arrives as bars, grain and old gold, and leaves the floor as jewellery, scrap and dust. Each lot should have a known purity. Scrap and filings are collected by department, weighed, and either reused or sent for refining, where the recovered fine gold is recorded against what was sent. A workshop that does not record recovery is treating recoverable gold as loss.

## Due dates and capacity

 Retailers judge a manufacturer on delivery. Each order should carry a due date, each job a stage and an expected finish, so that a late job is visible days before the retailer calls. Seeing every open job by stage and by karigar also shows where work is piling up before it becomes a missed delivery.

## Checklist for choosing manufacturing software

 Does it account in fine weight, with gross and purity shown?

 Can I set a wastage norm for each stage and be told when a job exceeds it?

 Does each karigar have an account in metal and money that he can see?

 Is client-supplied metal kept apart, client by client?

 Can I close metal for a department today, not at year end?

 Does the finished piece enter stock with its real weights and cost?

 Is the HUID attached piece by piece?

 Does the same system bill it, or must it be re-entered?

## How Jwero does it, and what it does not do

 Jwero runs orders, bills of materials, routings, issue and return in fine weight, wastage norms by stage, job cards, quality checks, hallmarking records, raw material lots and a karigar khata that settles wages against gold. Client-supplied metal is tracked as job work. Finished pieces go straight into the stock the counter and the trade desk sell from. Details are on the manufacturing page .

 It does not convert CAD files into bills of materials; these are entered by production. It does not yet run a full metal reconciliation or a physical metal count. It does not connect to casting machines or weighing equipment beyond the scales supported as devices.

## What jewellers ask about this.

 What is jewellery manufacturing software? 
 Software that follows precious metal through a workshop: orders, bills of materials, issue and return to karigars in fine weight, loss against norms at each stage, quality checks, hallmarking and finished stock.

 How is wastage calculated in jewellery making? 
 Metal issued for a job minus metal returned, including recovered scrap and dust, in fine weight. That loss is compared with the norm you have set for the stage.

 What is a karigar khata? 
 The account between a workshop and a craftsman: metal given to him, metal returned, the balance he holds and the wages due.

 Can it handle job work for other retailers? 
 Yes. Client-supplied metal and jobs are kept client by client, and invoices are raised for labour on the weights actually produced.

 Does it create a BOM from a CAD file? 
 No. In Jwero the bill of materials is entered by production. CAD to BOM conversion is not available.

 A visitor or enquirer You browse jwero.ai, use a calculator, chat or call us, or book a demonstration We decide how your data is used (data fiduciary)

 The jeweller using Jwero is called the “Customer” in this policy. If you are in a Customer’s records, their privacy notice applies to you, and requests about your data should go to them first. Section 9 explains how we help.

## 2. What we collect directly

 In plain words: Only what you give us or what is needed to run and secure the service.

 Enquiries. Name, phone number, email, business name, business type, city and what you tell us in chat, on a call or in a form.

 Accounts. Name, email, phone, password hash or the identifier from Google or LinkedIn sign-in, role, multi-factor and passkey credentials, session and device details and IP address.

 Billing. Business name, address, GSTIN, billing contact and payment references. Card and bank details are entered with the payment provider and are not stored by Jwero.

 Support. Messages, call notes and screen recordings you choose to share. If a call or video session is recorded, you are told at the start.

 This website. The site keeps a few preferences in your own browser, such as the kind of business you selected and the light or dark theme. These are not sent to our servers and you can clear them in your browser. The website does not run advertising trackers. If the chat widget is used, the conversation is handled in the Jwero application.

 Depending on which parts of Jwero a Customer uses, their workspace may contain:

## 4. How we use personal data

 In plain words: To answer you, to run the product, to bill for it and to keep it safe.

 To reply to enquiries and run demonstrations and trials.

 To create and secure accounts, and to provide, maintain and support the product.

 To bill, collect payment and meet tax and accounting obligations.

 To detect misuse, investigate incidents and keep audit records.

 To send service messages about your account. Marketing messages are sent only where you have agreed, and you can stop them at any time.

 To improve the product using operational measures such as usage counts and error reports. We do not use the content of a Customer’s records to train our own models.

 Data in a Customer’s workspace is processed only to provide the service to that Customer, on their instructions, as set out in the Data Policy .

## 5. Automated scoring and AI

 In plain words: Jwero scores customer activity to suggest who to contact, and AI drafts messages. A person approves what is sent.

 Scoring. Within a Customer’s workspace, Jwero reads customer activity, such as purchases, catalogue views, visits and scheme payments, and produces scores (for example likelihood to buy or risk of drifting away). Each score shows the reasons behind it. The scores suggest who a salesperson should contact. They do not decide prices, credit or eligibility on their own.

 AI drafting. AI features draft replies, summaries, content and images. To do this, the relevant conversation and record are sent to an AI model provider listed on the Sub-processors page, some of which process data outside India. Drafts wait for a person’s approval unless the Customer has enabled a specific kind of action to run within limits they set, and the Customer can stop AI activity at any time.

 If you are a jeweller’s customer and object to scoring or to AI-assisted messages, tell that jeweller. They can exclude your record.

## 6. Who receives personal data

 In plain words: Service providers that help us run the product, under contract. Nobody else, except where the law requires it.

 We share personal data with:

 Sub-processors that host, message, process payments, provide AI models or monitor the service. They are named, with their purpose and location, on the Sub-processors page.

 Services a Customer connects , such as Tally, Zoho Books, Shopify, marketplaces or advertising accounts. These receive data because the Customer has switched the connection on.

 Authorities , where a law, court order or lawful request requires it. We disclose only what is required and, unless prohibited, tell the Customer concerned.

 A successor , if the business is merged or sold, under terms no less protective than these.

 We do not sell personal data, and we do not let anyone use it for their own advertising.

## 7. Where data is stored and transferred

 In plain words: Primary hosting is in India. Some providers, mainly for AI and messaging, process data abroad.

 Workspaces are hosted on cloud infrastructure in India. Some sub-processors, in particular AI model providers, Meta and monitoring tools, process data in other countries. Transfers are made only to countries not restricted by the Government of India under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and under contracts that require the recipient to protect the data.

## 8. How long we keep it

 In plain words: As long as needed for the purpose, and as long as the law requires for tax and identity records.

 Data Kept for 
 Enquiries that do not become accounts Up to 24 months after the last contact, then deleted or anonymised 
 Account and billing records The life of the account, then as tax and company law require (generally eight years for books of account) 
 A Customer’s workspace The life of the subscription, and an export period after it ends, as set out in the Data Policy 
 Invoices, orders, payments, purchases and payroll inside a workspace Kept as statutory records. GST law requires 72 months from the due date of the annual return 
 Identity-check records For the period anti-money-laundering and tax law require, after which they are deleted 
 Security and activity logs Up to 12 months 

## 9. Your rights

 In plain words: You can ask to see, correct or delete your data, withdraw consent, complain and nominate someone to act for you.

 Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 you may:

 ask for a summary of the personal data being processed and what is being done with it;

 ask for it to be corrected, completed or updated;

 ask for it to be erased when it is no longer needed and no law requires it to be kept;

 withdraw consent, as easily as you gave it;

 nominate another person to exercise these rights if you die or lose capacity;

 raise a grievance with us, and if it is not resolved, with the Data Protection Board of India.

 If we hold your data directly , write to care@jwero.ai . We may need to confirm your identity first.

 If your data is in a jeweller’s Jwero account , ask that jeweller. The product gives them tools to export, correct and erase a person’s record and to record a withdrawal of consent. If you write to us instead, we will pass the request to the jeweller without delay and will not act on their data without their instruction.

 Some records cannot be erased on request because a law requires them to be kept, including tax invoices, payroll and identity-check records.

## 10. Security

 In plain words: Separate databases, encryption, tight access and tested backups. The detail is on the security page.

 Each Customer’s data is held in its own database, encrypted in transit and at rest, with role-based access, multi-factor login and audit records. Details, including what we have not yet achieved, are on the Security page. No system is perfectly secure. If a personal data breach occurs, we will notify the affected Customers, the people affected and the Data Protection Board of India as the law requires.

## 11. Children

 In plain words: Jwero is a business product and is not directed at children.

 We do not knowingly collect personal data from anyone under 18 through this website or as an account holder. A Customer may record a child’s name or date of birth as part of a family’s record, for example for a gift occasion. The Customer is responsible for obtaining a parent’s verifiable consent where the law requires it, and must not use Jwero to track children or target advertising at them.

## 12. Changes to this policy

 We will post changes here and change the date at the top. If a change materially affects how account holders’ data is used, we will tell account owners by email or in the product before it takes effect.

## 1. Who can use Jwero

 Jwero is offered to businesses and professionals for use in the course of their trade. It is not offered to consumers. You confirm that you are at least 18, that the information you give us is accurate, and that you have authority to bind the business you represent.

## 2. Your account

 In plain words: Keep logins personal and secure. The owner controls who gets access.

 The person who creates a workspace is its owner and may invite others and set their permissions. You are responsible for activity under your logins. Do not share a login between people. Turn on multi-factor login where you can, remove access promptly when someone leaves, and tell us at once if you suspect misuse.

## 3. The first month

 In plain words: There is no free trial. The first month is ₹3,600.

 A new workspace pays ₹3,600 for its first month of Jwero One instead of ₹18,000, with every module included. The first-month price applies once per business. From the second month the plan fee is ₹18,000 a month. Usage on the wallet is charged at the published rates from the first day.

## 4. Fees, the wallet and taxes

 In plain words: One plan fee in advance, usage at published rates, from a prepaid balance.

 Plan. The current fees are on the pricing page . The plan fee is charged monthly, in advance. Extra locations, registers, capacity and connected devices are charged at the published rates.

 Wallet. Fees and usage, including WhatsApp and SMS messages, AI, voice and video minutes and similar metered items, are debited from a prepaid wallet at the published rates. Rates set by third parties, such as Meta’s message charges, can change when they change theirs.

 If the balance runs out. When the wallet has no balance, the workspace becomes read-only until it is topped up. Your data is not deleted because of a low balance. If a subscription fee remains unpaid for seven days, the subscription is cancelled so that further fees stop accruing.

 Taxes. Fees exclude GST and other taxes, which are added at the applicable rate. We issue a tax invoice for each charge.

 Refunds. You may cancel at any time and the subscription then ends at the close of the period already paid for. Plan fees for a period that has started are not refunded, and moving to a lower plan mid-period does not create a refund. Wallet top-ups are prepaid. An unused paid balance is refunded where the law requires it or where we agree in writing; promotional credit is never refundable.

 Price changes. We will give at least 30 days’ notice of an increase in plan fees. It applies from your next renewal.

## 5. Your data

 In plain words: You own it. We process it for you. You can take it with you.

 You keep all rights in the data you and your users put into Jwero (“Customer Data”). You give us permission to host and process it only to provide and support the service, as described in the Data Policy , which forms part of these terms. You can export Customer Data in standard formats at any time.

 You are responsible for having the right to hold and use the personal data you put into Jwero, including giving notice to and obtaining consent from your customers, employees and others where the law requires it.

## 6. Acceptable use

 In plain words: Use it to run your business lawfully. Do not spam, break in or resell it.

 You must not, and must not allow anyone to:

 send messages to people who have not agreed to receive them, or in breach of the rules of WhatsApp, Meta, telecom regulations on commercial communications or any other channel;

 upload contact lists you have no right to use;

 use Jwero for anything unlawful, deceptive or infringing, or to record or track people without the notice or consent the law requires;

 probe, scan or test the service’s security without our written permission, or interfere with other customers’ use;

 copy, resell or reverse engineer the service, or use it to build a competing product;

 use automated means to extract data from the service other than through the export tools and connections we provide.

 We may suspend a workspace that is causing harm to others or putting the service at risk. Where we can, we will warn you first and give you the chance to put it right.

## 7. AI features

 In plain words: The AI drafts. Your people approve. What is sent is your message.

 Jwero includes AI that drafts replies, content, images, reports and suggested actions. AI output can be wrong or incomplete and should be checked. By default every AI-drafted action waits for a person’s approval. You may allow specific kinds of action to run without approval, within limits you set, and you can stop AI activity at any time.

 You are responsible for messages and actions your users approve or that run under settings you have enabled. As between you and Jwero, you own the output generated for you from your data. You must not use AI features to produce unlawful, deceptive or infringing content.

## 8. What Jwero is not

 In plain words: Software, not a regulated service or a professional adviser.

 Not financial services. Savings schemes, digital gold, girvi and loyalty programmes run in Jwero are offered by you to your customers. Jwero does not accept deposits, lend, hold customer money or gold, or act as your agent. You are responsible for any licence, registration, limit or filing that applies to those activities.

 Not tax, legal or accounting advice. Invoices, tax calculations, payroll and reports are produced from your settings and data. Check them with your own advisers. Jwero does not file returns for you.

 Not a certification. Recording a HUID, a certificate or an identity check in Jwero does not verify it.

 Not a guarantee of results. Calculators, estimates and examples on this website are illustrations based on the figures entered.

 Privacy Policy Terms of Use Data Policy Sub-processors DPDP statement Trust Centre 
 This policy sets out how Jwero handles the data a business puts into its workspace (“Customer Data”). It forms part of the Terms of Use and serves as the data processing terms between the Customer, as data fiduciary, and Jwero, as data processor, under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

 The short version

 You own your data. Jwero has no rights in it beyond running the service for you.
 One business, one database. Your records are never stored in the same database as another jeweller’s.
 We process your data only on your instructions, and our staff access it only to support you or keep the service running.
 You can export everything at any time, and for at least 30 days after you leave. Then it is deleted.
 If there is a breach affecting your data, we tell you without undue delay.

## 1. Ownership

 In plain words: Your customer list, your stock, your books: yours.

 Customer Data belongs to the Customer. Jwero does not claim ownership of it, does not sell it, and does not use it for any purpose other than providing, securing and supporting the service for that Customer. Jwero does not compare, combine or share one Customer’s data with another’s.

## 2. Roles

 For personal data in Customer Data, the Customer is the data fiduciary and Jwero is its data processor. The Customer decides what is collected and why. For account, billing and enquiry data, Jwero is the data fiduciary and the Privacy Policy applies.

## 3. What we process and why

 Subject matter Hosting and processing Customer Data to provide the Jwero service 
 Duration The subscription term and the export period after it 
 Purpose Running the modules the Customer uses: customer records, selling channels, counter, stock, purchase, manufacturing, schemes, HR, accounts, reports and AI assistance 
 People concerned The Customer’s customers and leads, employees and karigars, vendors and trade buyers, and visitors 
 Kinds of data As listed in section 3 of the Privacy Policy, including identity and financial identifiers where the Customer records them 

## 4. Our commitments as processor

 In plain words: We act on your instructions, keep it confidential, secure it and help you meet your obligations.

 Jwero will:

 process Customer Data only on the Customer’s documented instructions, which are these terms, the Customer’s settings and the actions its users take in the product;

 ensure that people authorised to access Customer Data are bound by confidentiality;

 apply the security measures in section 6;

 use sub-processors only as described in section 7;

 help the Customer respond to requests from individuals, through export, correction, erasure and consent tools in the product;

 notify the Customer of a personal data breach as described in section 10;

 delete or return Customer Data at the end of the service, as described in section 9;

 give the Customer the information reasonably needed to show that these commitments are being met.

## 5. The Customer’s responsibilities

 The Customer will:

 have a lawful basis for the personal data it puts into Jwero and give the notices the law requires, including that messages may be drafted with AI and that customer activity is scored;

 obtain consent before sending marketing messages, honour opt-outs, and obtain verifiable parental consent before processing a child’s data;

 tell employees and visitors about attendance location or photo capture, call recording and camera-based tracking where it enables them;

 record identity documents only where a law requires or permits it, and not store Aadhaar numbers or copies except as the law allows;

 set permissions so that staff see only what they need, and remove access when someone leaves.

## 6. Security measures

 In plain words: The measures in place today. The security page goes further.

 A separate database for each Customer.

 Encryption in transit and at rest; credentials and connection secrets encrypted.

 Role-based access with fine-grained permissions, multi-factor login and passkeys, single sign-on for larger deployments, and session revocation.

 Approval steps on financial records and a record of who changed what.

 Backups at a frequency and retention the Customer can set, with restore tests.

 Jwero staff access to a workspace limited to support and operations needs, and logged.

 A written incident response plan.

 Jwero does not hold SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification today. See Security for what is in place and what is planned.

## 7. Sub-processors

 In plain words: Named on a public page. We tell you before adding one.

 The Customer authorises Jwero to use the sub-processors listed on the Sub-processors page. Many are used only when the Customer switches on the feature that needs them. Jwero remains responsible for their work and requires them by contract to protect the data. We will update that page at least 15 days before adding a sub-processor that will handle Customer Data, and a Customer who objects may stop using the feature concerned or cancel.

## 8. Location and transfers

 Customer databases are hosted in India. Where a sub-processor processes data outside India, the transfer is made only to countries not restricted under Indian law and under contract. A Customer can avoid most transfers by not enabling the features that depend on providers abroad; the Sub-processors page shows which those are.

## 9. Retention, export and deletion

 In plain words: Export whenever you want. Statutory records are kept as long as the law says.

 During the subscription. Customer Data is kept for as long as the workspace is active. Operational logs and event history are kept for set periods, generally 90 to 365 days. Invoices, orders, payments, purchases, payroll and the ledger are statutory records and are not deleted on a schedule.

 Export. The Customer can export Customer Data in standard formats at any time, without asking us and at no charge.

 After the subscription ends. The workspace becomes read-only and remains available for export for at least 30 days. We then delete the database and its backups within a further 90 days, after writing to the workspace owner. A Customer may ask for earlier deletion in writing.

 What we may keep. Our own records of the account, invoices we issued and security logs, as the law requires.

## 10. Breach notification

 If Jwero becomes aware of a personal data breach affecting Customer Data, it will notify the workspace owner without undue delay, with what is known about what happened, the data involved and the steps being taken, and will keep the Customer updated. Jwero will give the Customer the information it needs to notify the Data Protection Board of India and the people affected.

## 11. Requests from individuals and authorities

 If an individual asks Jwero about data held in a Customer’s workspace, Jwero will refer the request to the Customer and will not respond on the Customer’s behalf without instruction. If an authority lawfully requires disclosure of Customer Data, Jwero will tell the Customer first unless the law forbids it, and will disclose only what is required.

## 12. Audit and assurance

 On reasonable written request, and not more than once a year unless there has been a breach, Jwero will provide its security overview and answer a Customer’s reasonable questionnaire. Enterprise customers may agree further audit rights in their order.

## 13. Contact

# DPDP Statement: Jwero and India’s Data Protection Act

How Jwero meets India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023: who is the data fiduciary and who the processor, notice and consent, the rights of data principals, children’s data, breach notification and grievance redressal.

## DPDP Statement

 Last updated 1 October 2026 · Tanika Tech Jewels Private Limited · CIN U74900MH2016PTC273631

 Privacy Policy Terms of Use Data Policy Sub-processors DPDP statement Trust Centre 
 This statement explains how Jwero applies India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (“the Act”) to the product and to this website. It should be read with the Privacy Policy and the Data Policy.

 The short version

 The jeweller is the data fiduciary for its customers’ and employees’ data. Jwero is its data processor.
 Jwero is the data fiduciary for its own account holders and enquirers.
 The product gives jewellers the tools the Act expects: consent records, opt-outs, export, correction and erasure.
 Grievances go to the Grievance Officer at care@jwero.ai.

 Roles under the Act 
 Notice and consent 
 Purpose and minimisation 
 Rights of data principals 
 Automated scoring 
 Children 
 Security safeguards and breaches 
 Processing outside India 
 Retention and erasure 
 Grievance Officer 

## 1. Roles under the Act

 Data Data fiduciary Data processor 
 A jeweller’s customers, employees, karigars, vendors and visitors The jeweller Jwero 
 Jwero account holders, billing contacts and enquirers Jwero Jwero’s sub-processors 

## 2. Notice and consent

 In plain words: The jeweller asks its own customers. The product records the answer.

 Where Jwero collects personal data directly, it gives notice at the point of collection of what is collected and why. Where a jeweller collects personal data through Jwero, giving notice and obtaining consent is the jeweller’s duty as data fiduciary. The product supports it: consent and channel preferences are recorded on each contact, opt-outs are enforced at the moment of sending, and messaging runs on Meta’s official business interfaces.

 Jewellers should check that contacts imported from older systems have agreed to receive marketing before sending to them.

## 3. Purpose and minimisation

 Jwero processes a jeweller’s data only to provide the service to that jeweller. Each jeweller chooses which fields to record. Identity documents and statutory identifiers should be recorded only where a law requires or permits it.

## 4. Rights of data principals

 Right How it is exercised 
 Access to a summary of data and processing The jeweller exports the person’s record from the product 
 Correction and updating The jeweller edits the record 
 Erasure The jeweller erases the record. Tax, payroll and identity-check records the law requires are retained 
 Withdrawal of consent Recorded on the contact and enforced before any message is sent 
 Nomination By writing to the jeweller, or to Jwero for account data 
 Grievance redressal To the jeweller for its records; to Jwero’s Grievance Officer for account and enquiry data 

## 5. Automated scoring

 The product scores customer activity to suggest who a salesperson should contact, and shows the reasons for each score. Jewellers should mention this in their own privacy notice. The scores do not decide prices, credit or eligibility on their own.

## 6. Children

 Jwero is not directed at children. Jewellers must obtain a parent’s verifiable consent before processing a child’s personal data and must not use the product to track children or direct advertising at them.

## 7. Security safeguards and breaches

 The safeguards are described in the Data Policy and on the Security page. In the event of a personal data breach, Jwero notifies affected jewellers without undue delay so that the Board and the people affected can be informed as the Act requires, and notifies the Board and affected people directly for data it holds as fiduciary.

## 8. Processing outside India

 Hosting is in India. Some sub-processors process data abroad, as shown on the Sub-processors page. Transfers are made only to countries not restricted by the Central Government under the Act.

## 9. Retention and erasure

 Personal data is erased when the purpose is served and no law requires it to be kept. Retention periods are in the Privacy Policy and the Data Policy.

## 10. Grievance Officer

 Grievance Officer, Tanika Tech Jewels Private Limited, Shop No. 14–15, Sagar Darshan Building 2, Geetanjali Nagar, Station Road, Bhayandar (West), Thane, Maharashtra 401101, India. Email care@jwero.ai , subject “DPDP”. Complaints are acknowledged within two working days and we aim to resolve them within thirty days. A data principal who is not satisfied may approach the Data Protection Board of India.

 They often involve:

 Production Milestones

 Quality Checks

 Delivery Coordination

 A single missed step can delay the entire project.

 Most custom jewellery projects follow a workflow similar to this:

 Customer Inquiry ↓ Requirement Discussion ↓ Design Proposal ↓ Quotation Approval ↓ CAD Design ↓ Customer Approval ↓ Production ↓ Quality Check ↓ Delivery

# Jewellery OMS vs ERP vs POS: What’s the Difference?

## Jewellery OMS vs ERP vs POS: What’s the Difference?

 As jewellery businesses grow, they often invest in multiple software systems to manage operations more effectively. However, many jewellers become

 All articles 

 Order management · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published 18 June 2026 · Reviewed October 2026 

 As jewellery businesses grow, they often invest in multiple software systems to manage operations more effectively.

 However, many jewellers become confused by the different technologies available.

 Terms like OMS, ERP , and POS are frequently used interchangeably, even though they serve very different purposes.

 This confusion often leads businesses to:

 Buy the wrong software

 Duplicate functionality

 Create disconnected workflows

 Miss operational opportunities

 Understanding the role of each system is critical.

 An Order Management System (OMS) , Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) platform, and Point of Sale (POS) system each solve different business challenges.

 In this guide, we’ll explain what each system does, where they overlap, and how modern jewellery businesses use them together. 

## Understanding the Three Systems

 Before comparing them, it’s important to understand their primary purpose.

 OMS (Order Management System) 

 Focuses on managing customer orders from creation through fulfilment and delivery.

 ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) 

 Manages core business operations such as inventory, procurement, finance, manufacturing , and accounting.

 POS (Point of Sale) 

 Handles retail transactions and customer purchases at physical locations.

 Each system plays a different role in the jewellery business ecosystem.

## What Does a Jewellery OMS Do?

 An OMS is designed to manage the complete lifecycle of customer orders. 

 Typical OMS responsibilities include:

 Order Capture

 Order Processing

 Order Tracking

 Custom Order Management

 Fulfilment Coordination

 Customer Communication

 Omnichannel Order Visibility

 A Jewellery OMS answers questions such as:

 Where is this order?

 Has production started?

 Is the order ready for dispatch?

 What is the fulfilment status?

 The OMS becomes the operational hub for customer orders.

## What Does a Jewellery ERP Do?

 ERP systems focus on internal business operations.

 Typical ERP functions include:

 Inventory Management 

 Procurement

 Manufacturing

 Accounting

 Finance

 Vendor Management

 Business Reporting

 An ERP answers questions such as:

 How much inventory is available?

 What materials need replenishment?

 What are current financial results?

 What is the production schedule?

 ERP systems provide operational control across the organization.

## What Does a Jewellery POS Do?

 A POS system is primarily designed for retail transactions.

 Functions typically include:

 Billing

 Payment Collection

 Customer Checkout

 Store Transactions

 Sales Recording

 Receipt Generation

 A POS answers questions such as:

 What products were sold?

 How much revenue was generated?

 What payment method was used?

 POS systems are optimized for in-store sales activities.

 Function OMS ERP POS

 Omnichannel Orders ✓ No No

 Accounting No ✓ No 
 Manufacturing No ✓ No

 Store Sales No No ✓ 
 Fulfilment Coordination ✓ Limited No 
 Customer Updates ✓ No No 
 
 Each platform solves a different problem.

## Why OMS Is Becoming More Important

 Customers now:

 Browse Online

 Enquire Through WhatsApp

 Visit Showrooms 

 Purchase Through Multiple Channels

 Expect Real-Time Updates

 Neither ERP nor POS systems were designed to manage these experiences.

 This is where OMS platforms provide value.

 They connect customer orders across channels and provide complete visibility throughout the order lifecycle.

## OMS Bridges the Gap Between ERP and POS

 A useful way to think about these systems is:

 Customer ↓ POS ↓ OMS ↓ ERP 

## POS

 Captures the sale.

## OMS

 Manages the order.

## ERP

 Supports fulfilment and operations.

 Retail Stores

 These orders often require:

 May start with POS.

 Growing Multi-Channel Businesses 

 Often add OMS.

 Larger Operations 

 Typically require ERP alongside OMS and POS.

 The right combination depends on business complexity and growth stage.

 You may need an OMS if:

 Orders come from multiple channels.

 Customers frequently request updates.

 Teams struggle with visibility.

 Custom orders are difficult to track.

 Unlike many retail products, jewellery orders often involve high-value items, customizations, certificates, size requirements, stone specifications, and customer approvals.

 Wrong design or product SKU selected.

 Wrong certificate attached to a product.

 As customer journeys become more connected, jewellery businesses face increasing pressure to manage orders efficiently across multiple channels.

 Unfortunately, many jewellers still rely on spreadsheets, WhatsApp chats, manual records, and disconnected systems to track customer orders.

 While these methods may work for smaller businesses, they quickly become difficult to manage as order volumes increase.

 This is why modern jewellers are investing in Order Management Systems (OMS). 

 An OMS helps businesses centralize order information , improve visibility, reduce errors, and deliver better customer experiences.

 In this guide, we’ll explore why order management has become essential for jewellery businesses and how an OMS helps support sustainable growth.

 Request customization

 All articles 

 Order management · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published 17 June 2026 · Reviewed October 2026 

 The jewellery industry has changed dramatically over the past decade.

 Customers no longer purchase exclusively through physical stores. They browse products online, enquire through WhatsApp, visit showrooms , compare designs, request customizations, and expect regular updates throughout the buying process.

 As a result, managing orders has become far more complex.

 A single jewellery order may involve multiple teams, systems, approvals, inventory checks, production processes, and customer interactions.

 Without a structured system, businesses often struggle with delays, communication gaps, order errors, and inconsistent customer experiences.

 This is where an Order Management System (OMS) becomes essential.

 A Jewellery OMS helps businesses manage every stage of the order lifecycle from order creation to fulfilment and delivery.

 In this guide, we’ll explain what a Jewellery Order Management System is, how it works, and why it has become a critical technology for modern jewellers.

## Understanding Order Management

 Order management refers to the process of receiving, processing, tracking, fulfilling, and delivering customer orders.

 For jewellery businesses, this process often includes:

 Customer Enquiries

 Order Creation

 Product Allocation

 Inventory Verification

 Custom Design Requests

 Production Tracking

 Delivery Coordination

 Customer Communication

 Every order follows a journey.

 The challenge is ensuring every stage is tracked accurately and completed efficiently.

## What Is a Jewellery Order Management System?

 A Jewellery Order Management System is software designed to manage and monitor the complete lifecycle of jewellery orders.

 It acts as a central platform where businesses can:

 Capture Orders

 Process Orders

 Track Order Status

 Manage Custom Orders

 Coordinate Fulfilment

 Communicate with Customers

 Monitor Delivery Progress

 Instead of managing orders through spreadsheets, WhatsApp messages, emails, and disconnected tools, businesses can manage everything from a single system.

## Why Jewellery Businesses Need an OMS

 Many jewellers begin with manual order management.

 Orders may be tracked using:

 Excel Sheets

 WhatsApp Messages

 Paper Records

 Shared Documents

 Individual Staff Knowledge

 These methods often work initially.

 However, as order volumes increase, businesses face challenges such as:

 Lost Orders

 Delayed Fulfilment

 Customer Complaints

 Inventory Conflicts

 Order Processing Errors

 Communication Breakdowns

 An OMS provides the structure needed to manage growth.

## How a Jewellery OMS Works

 A Jewellery OMS manages the entire order journey.

 A typical workflow looks like this:

 Customer Inquiry ↓ Order Creation ↓ Inventory Validation ↓ Approval Process ↓ Production / Allocation ↓ Fulfilment ↓ Delivery ↓ Customer Updates 
 Every stage becomes visible and manageable.

 This reduces confusion and improves accountability.

## Orders Come From Multiple Channels

 Today’s jewellery businesses receive orders from many sources.

 These may include:

 Retail Stores

 Ecommerce Websites 

 WhatsApp

 Instagram 

 Marketplaces 

 Sales Teams

 Franchise Locations

 Managing these channels separately creates operational complexity. 

 A Jewellery OMS centralizes orders into a single system.

 Unlike standard products, these orders often involve:

 Design Reviews

 Customer Approvals

 Delivery Milestones

 Customers increasingly expect transparency.

 Is my jewellery being manufactured?

 When will it be delivered?

 What is the current order status?

 Without an OMS, answering these questions often requires multiple phone calls and manual checks.

 Many of these issues occur because information is scattered across multiple systems.

 Businesses often experience:

 Inventory Visibility Issues

 An OMS helps synchronize order activity with inventory availability.

## What Are Generic Catalogue Tools ?

 Generic catalogue tools are systems designed to manage product information across multiple industries.

 Examples include:

 Basic Product Databases

 General Catalogue Platforms

 One Sales Channel

 More Products

 More Images

 Catalogue complexity increases exponentially.

 Purity

 Weight

 Gemstone Details

 Certification Information

 Ring Sizes

 Product DNA

 Generic tools often treat these as simple text fields.

 This creates inconsistency.

 A single jewellery product may exist in multiple versions.

 Examples include:

 Different Sizes

 Different Metals

 Different Stones

 Different Weights

 Different Purities

 Generic tools often create separate products for every variation.

 This causes:

 Duplicate Records

 Data Redundancy

 Reporting Challenges

 Catalog Bloat

 Jewellery products require extensive media assets.

 Examples include:

 Generic tools rarely include certificate management capabilities.

As jewellery businesses grow, managing products becomes increasingly complex. A retailer with 100 products can often manage information manually. A

PRODUCT DATA AND CATALOGUES

## Jewellery SKU Management: Complete Guide for Jewellers

 As jewellery businesses grow, managing products becomes increasingly complex. A retailer with 100 products can often manage information manually. A

 All articles 

 Product data and catalogues · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published 11 June 2026 · Reviewed October 2026 

 As jewellery businesses grow, managing products becomes increasingly complex.

 A retailer with:

 5,000 products

 Duplicate Products

 Reporting Challenges

 Operational Inefficiencies

 This is why successful jewellery businesses invest heavily in SKU management, variant SKU management, and product DNA structures.

 Together, these systems create the foundation for scalable product operations.

## What Is Jewellery SKU Management ?

 SKU stands for Stock Keeping Unit.

 A SKU is a unique identifier assigned to every product.

 It helps businesses:

 Track Products

 Manage Inventory

 Identify Variants

 Generate Reports

 Improve Accuracy

 Support Omnichannel Operations 

 Think of a SKU as a product’s unique identity within the business.

## Why SKU Management Is Critical for Jewellery Businesses

 Jewellery products are highly customizable.

 A single ring may exist in:

 Yellow Gold

 White Gold

 Rose Gold

 Different:

 Sizes

 Stone Types

 Diamond Qualities

 Collections

 Without structured SKU management, products become difficult to track.

## What Happens When SKU Management Fails?

 Many jewellery businesses experience:

 Duplicate SKUs

 Missing SKUs

 Manual SKU Creation

 Inconsistent Naming

 Inventory Errors

 Reporting Issues

 Variant Confusion

 The result is operational chaos.

## Understanding Jewellery Product DNA

 Before discussing variant SKUs, it is important to understand Product DNA.

 Product DNA is the core identity of a product.

 It remains consistent even when variations exist.

 For example:

 Product DNA:

 Solitaire Ring Collection

 The DNA remains the same.

 However, variations may include:

 Metal Type

 Ring Size

 Diamond Weight

 Stone Quality

 Color Option

 The DNA represents the parent product.

 Variants represent the children.

## Why Product DNA Matters

 Many jewellers manage every variation as a separate product.

 This creates:

 Duplicate Catalogue Entries

 Product Data Repetition

 Catalog Complexity

 Reporting Difficulties

 A Product DNA approach solves this.

## What Is a Variant SKU?

 A Variant SKU identifies a specific version of a product.

 Example:

 Product DNA

 SOL-RING

 Variants:

 SOL-RING-YG-16

 SOL-RING-WG-16

 SOL-RING-RG-16

 SOL-RING-YG-18

 SOL-RING-WG-18

 Each SKU represents a unique sellable product.

## Product DNA vs Variant SKU

 The easiest way to understand the difference:

## Product DNA

 Represents the master product.

## Variant SKU

 Represents a specific variation.

 Product DNA answers:

## What product is this?

 Variant SKU answers:

## Which exact version is this?

## Why Variant SKU Jewellery Management Is Difficult

 Jewellery businesses often manage:

 Metal Variants

 Size Variants

 Diamond Variants

 Gemstone Variants

 Weight Variants

 Custom Variants

 Without structure, SKU counts grow rapidly.

 A single product can generate dozens of variants.

## Common SKU Mistakes Jewellers Make

## 1. Manual SKU Creation

 Employees create SKUs differently.

 Examples:

 RING001

 RING-001

 RNG001

 Consistency disappears.

## 2. No Product DNA Structure

 Every variation becomes a separate product.

 Catalogues become bloated.

## 3. Duplicate SKUs

 Different products accidentally receive the same SKU.

 This creates inventory issues.

## 4. Overcomplicated SKUs

 Some businesses create SKUs that are impossible to understand.

 Complexity reduces usability.

## 5. No Governance Rules

 Without standards, SKU quality declines over time.

## Building a Jewellery SKU Framework

 A scalable SKU framework should include:

 Collection Identifier

 Product Category

 Product Type

 Variant Information

 Version Control

 Example:

 COL-RNG-SOL-YG-16

 This structure is:

 Consistent

 Searchable

 Scalable

 Easy to Understand

## Creating Product DNA Structures

 Every product should have:

 Parent Product

 ↓

 Product DNA

 ↓

 Variant Structure

 ↓

 Sellable SKUs

 This hierarchy improves catalogue organisation.

 Product data and catalogues · 6 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published 11 June 2026 · Reviewed October 2026 

 As jewellery businesses grow, product information starts appearing everywhere.

 A product may exist in:

 Ecommerce Website 

 WhatsApp Catalogue

 Marketplace Listings

 Shared Drives

 But over time, a serious problem emerges.

 Different teams begin using different versions of the same product information.

 The website shows one price.

 The store sees another.

 The WhatsApp catalogue contains outdated information.

 Marketing uses old images.

 Sales teams reference different specifications.

 This creates confusion, inefficiency, and lost sales.

 The solution is building a Single Source of Truth (SSOT) for jewellery product data.

## What Is a Single Source of Truth?

 A Single Source of Truth (SSOT) is a centralised system where all product information is stored, managed, validated, and distributed.

 Instead of maintaining product information across multiple disconnected systems, businesses maintain one master record.

 Every channel receives product information from that central source.

 This creates:

 Consistency

 Accuracy

 Trust

 Operational Efficiency

 Scalability

## Why Jewellery Businesses Need a Single Source of Truth

 Jewellery products are information-rich.

 A single product may contain:

 Product Name

 SKU

 Collection

 Gold Purity

 Metal Weight

 Diamond Specifications

 Gemstone Details

 Certifications

 Product Images

 Videos

 Pricing

 Product Descriptions 

 SEO Metadata

 Product Variants

 Managing this information across multiple systems creates risk.

## The Hidden Cost of Disconnected Product Data

 When product information is stored in multiple locations, businesses face:

 Duplicate Work

 Product Data Errors

 Inconsistent Catalogs

 Slow Product Updates

 Inventory Confusion

 Customer Frustration

 Reduced Trust

 Lower Conversions

 These problems compound as the business grows.

## What Happens Without a Single Source of Truth?

 Consider a common scenario.

 A new diamond ring is launched.

 The merchandising team updates:

## ERP

 The ecommerce team updates:

## Website

 The sales team updates:

## WhatsApp Catalogue

 The marketing team updates:

## Product Brochure

 Soon, every channel contains slightly different information.

 The result is product data chaos.

## Why Product Data Becomes Fragmented

 Most jewellery businesses evolve gradually.

 Different systems are introduced over time.

 For example:

 ERP for Operations

 Ecommerce Platform for Online Sales

 CRM for Customer Management

 WhatsApp for Sales

 Excel for Product Tracking

 Each system stores product information.

 Eventually, nobody knows which version is correct.

## What Should a Jewellery Product Master Include?

 The jewellery product master becomes the foundation of your source of truth.

 Product Name

 SKU

 Gemstone Information

 Product Variants 

 Product Relationships

 Everything should exist in one controlled location.

## The Difference Between Data Storage and Data Ownership

 Many businesses believe storing data in multiple systems creates redundancy.

 In reality, it creates confusion.

 A Single Source of Truth does not mean every system disappears.

 It means one system owns the product information.

 Other systems consume it.

 This distinction is critical.

 However, one of the most overlooked reasons for lost sales is something happening behind the scenes:

 Product Data Chaos 

 When product information is inconsistent across websites, stores, WhatsApp catalogues, ecommerce platforms, and sales teams, customer trust breaks down.

 Customers become confused.

 Sales teams lose confidence.

 Marketing campaigns become less effective.

 Conversions drop.

 In today’s omnichannel jewellery environment, product data is no longer just operational information.

 It directly impacts revenue.

## What Is Jewellery Product Data Chaos?

 Jewellery product data chaos occurs when different systems contain different versions of the same product information. 

 For example:

 A customer sees a diamond ring on your website.

 The website shows:

 Price: ₹98,500

 Weight: 12.5 grams

 IGI Certified

 Then the customer messages your team on WhatsApp.

 The salesperson shares:

 Price: ₹95,000

 Weight: 11.8 grams

 Certification Not Mentioned

 Later, the customer visits the showroom .

 The store team provides:

 Price: ₹99,500

 Different Product Images

 Different Specifications

 At this point, the customer starts questioning the credibility of the retailer.

 The issue is not pricing.

 The issue is trust.

## Why Product Data Has Become More Complex

 Twenty years ago, jewellery businesses only needed to manage product information in stores.

 Today, products must appear consistently across:

 Ecommerce Website 

 WhatsApp Catalogue 

 Instagram 

 Facebook Shops

 Marketplace Listings

 Retail Stores

 Sales Team Catalogues

 CRM Systems

 Every channel requires accurate product information.

 The more channels a business uses, the more difficult product management becomes.

 Sales teams often rely on manually maintained catalogues.

 Without centralised product data:

 Store teams need accurate information to:

 Advise Customers

 Verify Pricing

 Check Inventory

 Build Trust

 If store information differs from what customers saw online, credibility immediately suffers.

## Why Spreadsheets Fail for Jewellery Product Management

 Many jewellery businesses begin their product management journey with spreadsheets. It makes sense. Spreadsheets are familiar, inexpensive, and easy to

 All articles 

 Product data and catalogues · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published 11 June 2026 · Reviewed October 2026 

 Many jewellery businesses begin their product management journey with spreadsheets.

 It makes sense.

 Spreadsheets are familiar, inexpensive, and easy to set up. A jeweller can create columns for product names, SKUs, gold purity, diamond details, pricing, and inventory quantities within minutes.

 For a small catalogue of 50 or 100 products, spreadsheets often seem sufficient.

 The problem starts when the business grows.

 A modern jewellery retailer may manage thousands of products across multiple collections, categories, locations, and sales channels. Product information must be synchronised across websites, ecommerce stores, WhatsApp catalogues, marketplaces , sales teams, and physical stores.

 At this stage, spreadsheets stop being a productivity tool and start becoming a business risk.

 This is why many growing jewellery businesses eventually abandon spreadsheet-based product management and move to dedicated Product Information Management (PIM) platforms.

## Why Jewellery Product Data Is More Complex Than Other Retail Industries

 Most retail products have relatively simple data requirements.

 Jewellery products are different.

 A single jewellery product may include:

 Product Name

 SKU

 Collection Name

 Product Category

 Gold Purity

 Metal Weight

 Diamond Weight

 Diamond Clarity

 Diamond Color

 Gemstone Details

 Certification Information

 Product Images

 Product Videos

 Pricing

 Making Charges

 SEO Metadata

 Product Descriptions

 Product Variants

 Now imagine managing this information for:

 5,000 products

 20 collections

 3 store locations

 Ecommerce website 

 WhatsApp catalogue

 Marketplace listings

 The complexity grows exponentially.

## Problem 1: Spreadsheet Data Errors Are Inevitable

 One of the biggest risks of a jewellery product management spreadsheet is human error.

 Every manual update creates opportunities for mistakes.

 Common jewellery product data errors include:

 Incorrect Pricing

 Wrong SKU Assignment

 Missing Product Images

 Incorrect Purity Information

 Duplicate Products

 Missing Certifications

 Broken Product Links

 Even a single pricing mistake can affect customer trust and profitability.

 Unlike a dedicated PIM system, spreadsheets do not validate data automatically.

 The responsibility falls entirely on employees.

## Problem 2: Multiple Spreadsheet Versions Create Chaos

 Most jewellery businesses eventually experience this scenario:

 Someone creates:

 Product_Master.xlsx

 Then:

 Product_Master_Final.xlsx

 Then:

 Product_Master_Final_v2.xlsx

 Then:

 Product_Master_Updated_Final.xlsx

 Soon, nobody knows which file is correct.

 Marketing uses one version.

 Ecommerce uses another version.

 Sales teams reference a different version.

 The result is inconsistent product information across the business.

## Problem 3: Jewellery Catalogue Spreadsheet Problems Increase as the Catalogue Grows

 A spreadsheet may work for:

## 100 Products

 It becomes difficult for:

## 1,000 Products

 It becomes nearly impossible for:

## 10,000 Products

 Searching, filtering, updating, and maintaining large catalogues through spreadsheets consumes significant time.

 Every new collection adds complexity.

 Every new product variant increases maintenance requirements.

 Catalogue management eventually becomes a full-time administrative task.

## Problem 4: Images, Videos and Certificates Cannot Be Managed Properly

 Modern jewellery selling relies heavily on visual content.

 Customers expect:

 High-Resolution Images

 Product Videos

 Diamond Certificates

 Hallmark Documents

 Lifestyle Photography

 Product Brochures

 Spreadsheets cannot manage these assets effectively.

 Most businesses end up storing files across:

 Google Drive

 Dropbox

 Shared Folders

 Employee Systems

 This creates fragmentation and inefficiency.

## Problem 5: Omnichannel Commerce Breaks Spreadsheet Workflows

 Today’s jewellery customer moves between:

 Website

 WhatsApp

 Instagram 

 Marketplace

 Retail Store

 Sales Consultant

 The customer expects the same information everywhere.

 However, spreadsheets are not designed for omnichannel product distribution.

 Updating product information in a spreadsheet does not automatically update:

 Ecommerce listings

 WhatsApp catalogues 

 Sales applications

 Marketplace listings

 This creates inconsistencies that damage trust.

## Problem 6: No Product Approval Workflow

 Modern product management requires governance.

 Before a product goes live, businesses often need:

 Product Review

 Content Validation

 Image Approval

 Pricing Approval

 Compliance Checks

 Spreadsheets offer no structured approval process.

 Anyone with access can modify critical product information.

## Problem 7: No Product Completeness Monitoring

 How many products are missing images?

 Which products do not have SEO descriptions?

 Which products lack certification data?

 Which products have incomplete attributes?

 A spreadsheet cannot answer these questions automatically.

 A dedicated PIM platform can.

 This becomes increasingly important as catalogues grow.

## Problem 8: Jewellery Inventory Spreadsheet Limitations

 Many jewellers attempt to use spreadsheets for inventory visibility.

 This creates additional problems.

 Inventory spreadsheets struggle with:

 Real-Time Updates

 Multi-Store Visibility

 Inventory Synchronization

 Product Variants 

 Omnichannel Stock Availability

 Inventory Forecasting

 As inventory complexity grows, spreadsheets become unreliable.

## Problem 9: Team Collaboration Becomes Difficult

 Product management involves multiple departments:

 Merchandising

 Marketing

 Ecommerce

 Retail Operations

 Sales

 Inventory Teams

 Managing collaboration through spreadsheets creates bottlenecks.

 Employees overwrite changes.

 Information gets lost.

 Version conflicts increase.

 Product launches slow down.

## Problem 10: Spreadsheets Are Not Built for Growth

 Every growing jewellery business eventually faces:

 More Products

 More Channels

 More Stores

 More Employees

 More Customers

 More Product Variants

 Spreadsheets do not scale effectively.

 What worked at 100 products rarely works at 10,000 products.

## The Hidden Cost of Spreadsheet Management

 Many businesses assume spreadsheets are free.

 They are not.

 The hidden costs include:

 Employee Time

 Product Errors

 Delayed Product Launches

 Customer Complaints

 Revenue Loss

 Catalog Inconsistency

 Duplicate Work

 Lost Opportunities

 These costs often exceed the cost of implementing proper software.

 Product Information Management (PIM) software was designed specifically to solve these problems.

 A Jewellery PIM provides:

 Product data and catalogues · 5 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published 10 June 2026 · Reviewed October 2026

## What Is Jewellery PIM?

 Jewellery PIM (Product Information Management) is a centralised platform that helps jewellery businesses manage, organise, enrich, and distribute product information across multiple sales channels.

 A Jewellery PIM becomes the single source of truth for all product-related information.

 This includes:

 Product Names

 Product Descriptions

 Images

 Videos

 SKU Data

 Pricing

 Inventory Attributes

 Metal Specifications

 Diamond Details

## What metrics should be tracked?

 Metrics like Conversion rate, pipeline value, appointment rate, revenue forecast, and lead response time should be tracked by jewellers.

 Ecommerce and websites · 3 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published 8 June 2026 · Reviewed October 2026 

 Successful jewellery stores do not rely on individual employees to deliver consistent performance.

 They rely on systems .

 Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) help retailers create consistency across customer interactions, sales processes, follow-ups, appointments , and store operations.

 Without SOPs, businesses often experience:

 Inconsistent customer experiences

 Missed leads

 Poor follow-ups

 Staff dependency

 Operational inefficiencies

 This guide explains the most important SOPs every jewellery retailer should implement.

## What Are SOPs?

 Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are documented processes that define how tasks should be completed.

 They ensure every team member follows the same process.

 Benefits include:

 Consistency

 Accountability

 Better Customer Experience

 Improved Productivity

 Faster Staff Training 

 Scalable Growth

## Why SOPs Matter in Jewellery Retail

 Jewellery purchases involve:

 High-value transactions

 Multiple interactions

 Long decision cycles

 Personalized consultations

 A structured process improves conversion rates and customer satisfaction.

## Core SOPs Every Jewellery Store Needs

## 1. Lead Management SOP 

 Every lead should follow a standard process.

 Lead Received

 ↓

 Assigned to Staff

 ↓

 ↓

 Qualification

 ↓

 Appointment Booking

 ↓

 Follow-Up

 ↓

 This ensures consistency.

RETAIL OPERATIONS AND SALES

## Jewellery Retail KPIs Every Owner Should Track

 Successful jewellery businesses are built on data-driven decisions. Many retailers focus only on revenue, but revenue alone does not reveal

 All articles 

 Retail operations and sales · 3 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published 8 June 2026 · Reviewed October 2026 

 Successful jewellery businesses are built on data-driven decisions. 

 Many retailers focus only on revenue, but revenue alone does not reveal the full picture.

 To improve performance, jewellery store owners must track key performance indicators ( KPIs ) that measure sales, customer behaviour, operational efficiency, and profitability.

 This guide covers the most important KPIs every jewellery retailer should monitor.

## What Are KPIs?

 KPIs (Key Performance Indicators) are measurable metrics that help businesses evaluate performance.

 They answer questions such as:

 Are sales improving?

 Are leads converting?

 Are customers returning?

 Is the team performing effectively?

 Are marketing campaigns working?

 KPIs provide visibility into business health.

## Why KPI Tracking Matters

 Tracking KPIs helps jewellery retailers:

 Improve Sales Performance

 Increase Conversion Rates

 Identify Bottlenecks

 Improve Customer Retention

 Measure Team Productivity

 Increase Profitability

 Businesses that measure performance consistently make better decisions.

## Revenue KPIs

## Total Revenue

 The most basic performance metric.

 Measures:

 Daily revenue

 Weekly revenue

 Monthly revenue

 Annual revenue

 Revenue trends help identify growth opportunities.

## Revenue Growth Rate

 Formula:

 Revenue Growth % = (Current Revenue, Previous Revenue) ÷ Previous Revenue × 100

 Measures business growth over time.

## Average Order Value (AOV)

 Formula:

 Total Revenue ÷ Number of Orders

 Higher AOV increases profitability.

## Sales Performance KPIs

## Conversion Rate 

 Formula:

 Purchases ÷ Leads × 100

 Measures how effectively enquiries become customers.

## Appointment Conversion Rate

 Formula:

 Purchases ÷ Appointments × 100

 Shows the effectiveness of consultations and showroom visits.

## Walk-In Conversion Rate

 Formula:

 Purchases ÷ Walk-In Visitors × 100

 Measures in-store sales performance.

## Lead Management KPIs

## Total Leads Generated

 Track leads from:

 Google Ads 

 Facebook Ads

 Instagram

 WhatsApp

 Referrals

 Lead volume drives future sales.

## Lead Response Time 

 Measures how quickly staff respond to enquiries.

 Faster responses improve conversion rates.

## Lead-to-Appointment Rate 

 Formula:

 Appointments ÷ Leads × 100

 Shows the effectiveness of lead nurturing.

## Customer KPIs

## Repeat Purchase Rate

 Formula:

 Repeat Customers ÷ Total Customers × 100

 Measures customer retention.

## Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) 

 Measures total revenue generated by a customer over time.

 Higher CLV indicates stronger customer relationships.

## Customer Retention Rate

 Measures how effectively customers return.

 Retention drives long-term profitability.

## Appointment KPIs

## Total Appointments Booked

 Tracks appointment volume.

## Appointment Attendance Rate

 Formula:

 Attended Appointments ÷ Booked Appointments × 100

 Shows appointment quality.

## Appointment-to-Purchase Rate 

 Measures the effectiveness of consultations.

## Marketing KPIs

## Cost Per Lead (CPL)

 Formula:

 Marketing Spend ÷ Leads Generated

 Measures campaign efficiency.

## Return on Ad Spend (ROAS)

 Formula:

 Revenue Generated ÷ Advertising Spend

 Measures advertising profitability.

## Campaign Conversion Rate

 Tracks performance of individual campaigns.

## Staff Performance KPIs

## Sales Per Staff Member

 Measures productivity.

## Conversion Rate by Staff Member 

 Identifies top performers.

## Revenue Generated Per Employee

 Measures contribution to sales.

## Follow-Up Completion Rate

 Tracks operational discipline.

## Inventory & Product KPIs

## Best-Selling Categories

 Examples:

 Gold jewellery

 Diamond jewellery 

 Bridal collections

## Inventory Turnover

 Measures how quickly stock is sold.

## Product Performance

 Tracks sales by category and collection.

## KPI Dashboard Example

 A jewellery retailer should ideally monitor:

 Revenue

 Conversion Rate

 Lead Response Time

 Appointment Rate 

 Repeat Purchase Rate

 Customer Lifetime Value

 Staff Performance

 Marketing ROI

 These KPIs provide a complete business view.

## Common KPI Tracking Mistakes

 Tracking Too Many Metrics

 Ignoring Customer KPIs

 No Lead Tracking

 No Staff Accountability

 Inconsistent Reporting

 No CRM Integration 

 Focus on metrics that directly impact growth.

## How CRM Improves KPI Visibility

 CRM helps retailers:

 Track leads

 This creates operational visibility.

## Final Thoughts

 Jewellery retailers cannot improve what they do not measure.

 By tracking the right KPIs consistently, businesses can:

 Increase sales

 Improve conversions

 Retain more customers

 Improve operational efficiency

 Grow profitability

 Data-driven retailers consistently outperform competitors.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

## What is the most important KPI for jewellery retailers?

 Conversion rate is one of the most important metrics because it directly impacts revenue.

## Why is lead response time important?

 Faster responses typically result in higher conversion rates.

## What KPI measures customer loyalty?

 Repeat Purchase Rate and Customer Lifetime Value.

## How often should KPIs be reviewed?

 Daily for operational KPIs and monthly for strategic KPIs.

## How can CRM help with KPI tracking?

 CRM centralises customer, lead, appointment, and sales data for reporting.

## What KPIs should small jewellery stores track first?

 Revenue, conversion rate, lead response time, appointment rate, and repeat purchase rate.

 All articles 

 Product data and catalogues · 3 min read · By the Jwero editorial team · Published 6 June 2026 · Reviewed October 2026 

 Most jewellery retailers focus heavily on website design and product photography.

 However, even the best-looking jewellery website will struggle to generate sales if customers cannot find it on Google.

 Product Page SEO helps jewellery stores attract qualified traffic, improve visibility, and increase conversions.

 This guide explains how to optimise jewellery product pages for both search engines and customers.

## Why Product Page SEO Matters

 A well-optimised product page can:

 Increase Organic Traffic

 Improve Product Visibility

 Generate Qualified Leads

 Boost Ecommerce Sales

 Reduce Advertising Dependence

 For many jewellery brands , SEO becomes one of the highest ROI marketing channels.

## Understanding Jewellery Search Intent

 Customers search differently depending on where they are in the buying journey.

 Examples:

 Diamond Engagement Rings

 Gold Necklace for Wedding

 Bridal Jewellery Collection 

 Daily Wear Gold Earrings

 Solitaire Ring Price

 Your product pages should align with customer search intent.

## 1. Optimise Product Titles

 The product title is one of the most important SEO elements.

 Good example:

 22K Gold Bridal Necklace Set 

 Poor example:

 Model 1024 

 Always include:

 Product Type

 Material

 Key Attribute

 Occasion (if relevant)

## 2. Write Unique Product Descriptions

 Avoid copying manufacturer descriptions.

 Good descriptions should include:

 Product Features

 Material Information

 Design Details

 Usage Occasions

 Customer Benefits

 Unique content helps search engines understand the page.

## 3. Use High-Quality Images

 Images improve both SEO and conversions.

 Best practices:

 Multiple Angles

 Zoom Capability

 Optimised File Sizes 

 Descriptive Image Names

 Alt Text

 Example:

 22k-gold-bridal-necklace.jpg 

 instead of

 IMG1234.jpg 

## 4. Optimise Meta Titles

 Meta titles should include primary keywords.

 Example:

 22K Gold Bridal Necklace Set | Jewellery Store Name 

 Keep titles clear and descriptive.

## 5. Optimise Meta Descriptions

 Meta descriptions influence click-through rates.

 Example:

 “Explore our 22K Gold Bridal Necklace Collection with certified craftsmanship and elegant designs.”

 Well-written descriptions increase traffic.

## 6. Use SEO-Friendly URLs

 Good URL:

 /gold-bridal-necklace-set 

 Poor URL:

 /product?id=58291 

 Short, descriptive URLs perform better.

## 7. Add Structured Data

 Schema markup helps Google understand products.

 Useful schema:

 Product Schema 

 Review Schema

 FAQ Schema

 Breadcrumb Schema

 Structured data improves search visibility.

## 8. Include Customer Reviews

 Reviews provide:

 Fresh Content

 Trust Signals 

 Additional Keywords

 Better Conversions

 Google also values user-generated content.

## 9. Improve Internal Linking

 Link related products and collections.

 Examples:

 Matching Earrings

 Bridal Collections 

 Diamond Jewellery 

 Gold Collections

 Internal links help search engines discover content.

## 10. Optimise Category Pages

 Many jewellery category pages rank better than individual products.

 Important categories:

 Gold Jewellery 

 Diamond Jewellery

 Bridal Jewellery

 Rings

 Earrings

 Necklaces

 Each category should have unique content.

## 11. Improve Page Speed

 Page speed directly impacts:

 SEO

 User Experience

 Conversion Rate

 Optimize:

 Images

 Hosting

 Code

 Mobile Performance

 Fast websites rank better.

## 12. Mobile SEO Matters

 Most jewellery traffic comes from mobile devices.

 Ensure:

 Mobile-Friendly Design

 Fast Loading

 Easy Navigation

 Mobile Checkout

 Click-to-WhatsApp 

 Mobile optimisation is now essential.

## Common Product Page SEO Mistakes

 Duplicate Product Descriptions

 Poor Product Titles

 Missing Meta Tags

 Slow Website Speed

 Weak Internal Linking

 No Structured Data

 Poor Mobile Experience

 Avoiding these mistakes improves rankings.

## Product Page SEO Checklist

 ✅ SEO-Friendly Product Title

 ✅ Unique Description

 ✅ Optimised Images

 ✅ Meta Title

 ✅ Meta Description

 ✅ Structured Data

 ✅ Customer Reviews

 ✅ Internal Links

 ✅ Fast Page Speed

 A poorly implemented CRM becomes another unused software tool.

 A CRM becomes the foundation for:

 Customer engagement

 Lead management 

 Follow-ups

 Customer intelligence 

 Loyalty programs 

 Repeat sales

 Poor visibility

 A customer may enquire about:

 Engagement rings

 Bridal jewellery

 Diamond necklaces

 Gold investments

 Anniversary gifts

 They show interest

 They ask questions

 They explore options

 Then silence follows

 Not from the customer, from the business

 In jewellery retail, effective follow-up is often the difference between an enquiry and a sale.

## Why Follow-Up Matters in Jewellery Retail

 Jewellery purchases rarely happen instantly.

 Customers often need time to:

 Compare products

 Discuss options with family

 Evaluate budgets

 Consider designs

 Explore alternatives

 This means most customers require multiple interactions before making a decision.

 Businesses that remain present throughout the decision process are more likely to win the sale.

## What Is Customer Follow-Up?

 Customer follow-up is the process of continuing engagement after an initial interaction.

 The purpose is to:

 Maintain interest

 Answer questions

 Build trust

 Guide decision-making

 Encourage purchase readiness

 Good follow-up creates value.

 Bad follow-up creates pressure.

## Common Follow-Up Problems

 Many jewellery retailers experience:

## Forgotten Enquiries

 No one remembers to follow up.

## Inconsistent Communication

 Every team member follows a different process.

## Excessive Messaging

 Customers feel pressured.

## Poor Timing

 Messages arrive too late.

## No Visibility

 Managers cannot see follow-up activity.

 These issues reduce conversion rates.

## The Ideal Jewellery Follow-Up Process

## Step 1: Immediate Response

 The first response should happen quickly.

 Customers increasingly expect:

 Fast answers

 Product information

 Helpful guidance

 Speed creates trust.

## Step 2: Qualification 

 Understand:

 Product interest

 Budget expectations

 Purchase timeline

 Occasion

 This helps personalise future interactions.

## Step 3: Value-Based Engagement

 Follow-ups should provide value.

 Examples:

 Product recommendations

 Design options

 Collection highlights

 Educational content

 Every interaction should help the customer.

## Step 4: Purchase Support

 Customers often need reassurance.

 Follow-ups can address:

 Product comparisons

 Pricing questions

 Customization options

 Appointment scheduling

 This reduces purchase friction.

## Step 5: Post-Purchase Follow-Up

 Follow-up does not end after the sale.

 Businesses should continue engagement through:

 Thank-you messages

 Care guidance

 Loyalty programs 

 Occasion reminders

 This supports long-term relationships.

## Why Timing Matters

 The same message can produce very different results depending on timing.

 Good timing improves:

 Response rates

 Engagement

 Conversion

 Poor timing often leads to disengagement.

 CRM systems help businesses manage timing more effectively.

## What Is Customer Segmentation?

 Rather than managing one large customer database, businesses create smaller customer groups with similar behaviours, interests, and needs.

 Improve personalization

 Increase engagement

 Deliver relevant communication

 Improve marketing performance

 Increase customer retention

 Lower engagement

 Missed opportunities

 Repeat buyers

 A CRM system is software designed to help businesses:

 Store customer information

 Track interactions

 Manage enquiries

 Improve communication

 Build long-term relationships

# How AI Is Changing the Jewellery Business
